- `EffectIntentHomeV1` is exactly `ActiveStoreHomeV1 | NoStoreCeremonyHomeV1 | PreStoreCeremonyHomeV1`. Active Store binds one stable RepositoryDomain or InstallationDomain identity and semantic namespace; No Store is only `InstallationContextGenesis` and fabricates no active domain, Generation or Epoch; Pre Store binds one exact inactive Repository or Installation Ceremony branch.
- Every Intent records one immutable **EffectIntentOriginationFenceV1**. Every later DispatchAttempt or Action-origin ReconciliationAttempt supplies one fresh same-home **EffectIntentUseFenceV1**; a new Generation or Epoch never validates an old use fence and never reparents the Intent.
- Home-qualified semantic uniqueness is enforced inside the one owning Store or sealed Ceremony branch. Another domain may hold only a non-bearer reference; there is no cross-domain Intent, Control Head, writer term, provider key, lock, transaction or global deduplication claim.
- One **Step Effect Origin** binds one exact Step Binding, StepAttempt, StepLease fence, and current LeaseTerm at the origination commit. Once committed, every Step reference is provenance only and the Intent survives Lease, Attempt, Run, Step membership, Contract amendment, terminal Work, process, and Session.
- One **Coordination Delivery Origin** binds one immutable Message, logical recipient, exact Delivery Subject, and purpose hash. One Message may source 0..N Intents, one per exact recipient-subject-purpose tuple, and at most one live Intent represents the same tuple. A changed recipient, subject, or purpose is a new explicitly authorized semantic operation.
- One **Effect Remediation Origin** binds one prior Effect Intent, cancels or compensates, and one remediation semantic-subject hash. The origin graph is self-edge-free, creation-ordered, acyclic, and semantically unique.
- Only Step Effect Origin may encode Work, Contract Root, Step, Lease, or LeaseTerm origin fields. Coordination Delivery Origin and Effect Remediation Origin encode none and inherit no Step authority, applicability, lifecycle, mutation right, or blocker scope.
- One Effect Intent binds exactly one semantic-operation hash and **Provider Operation Contract**. Two live Intents cannot represent the same semantic remote operation.
- One Effect Intent owns 0..N **Dispatch Attempts** and exactly one current home-local **Effect Intent Control Head**. Evidence owns the 0..N remote Observations and reconciliation Assessments that reference the Intent; those references grant no Intent writer, currentness or classification authority. The Head-selected revision contains zero or one live dispatch and one immutable Remote Classification revision; neither is independently current.
- Dispatch reservation commits before connector I/O. No network call occurs inside the canonical SQLite transaction.
- Maestro Action Request idempotency and provider idempotency are distinct. Safe redispatch reuses the same Intent, semantic hash, provider scope, and provider key.
- A possible dispatch without conclusive Observation becomes in_doubt. Timeout, cancellation, process exit, Lease expiry, HTTP acceptance, amendment, or Step removal cannot classify remote truth.
- Remote reconciliation may use narrower read-only authority and credential scope than dispatch, but still requires both live Maestro authority and an available Connector Credential Binding.
- Callback, response, poll, signed receipt, and human adjudication enter as typed Observations; pinned reconciliation preserves conflicts and never prefers newest.
- A **Compensation Intent** is a distinct Effect Intent with Effect Remediation Origin and independent authority, credentials, provider key, dispatch fence, budget, uncertainty, and reconciliation. It never mutates the original Intent or inherits the original origin authority.
- Pending, in_doubt, partially_applied, conflicted, or otherwise unresolved effects survive origin removal and block duplicate or unsafe operations and migration activation. They block Step Submission or Work completion only when their Step Effect Origin is current-material or an independently published Contract or Gate makes that effect material; remediation lineage alone neither clears nor inherits blocker scope.
- External schedulers may invoke advertised effect actions through Packet and authority contracts but never own Intent state, retry policy, credentials, or lifecycle.

- One **StepLease** is paired with exactly one **StepAttempt**, and one StepAttempt with exactly one StepLease. Acquisition and terminal disposition publish both atomically; neither exists or reopens alone.
- One live pair has exactly one current immutable **Lease Term** head. Renewal appends one contiguous term; it never changes the fence, executor Principal, binding, root, envelope, hard deadline, or cumulative budgets.
- At most one StepLease-StepAttempt pair is effectively live for one Step Binding at one as_of. A successor pair advances the stable Step fence high-water and links its predecessor without transferring authority or Runs.
- One StepAttempt belongs to exactly one verified executor Principal and owns 0..N finite bounded Step-execution Runs. Session refresh for that Principal changes request authentication, not Attempt identity.
- One **Run** belongs to exactly one ExecutionAttempt for life, has one immutable semantic-operation identity and one terminal outcome, and is never reopened, reparented, or promoted from uninstrumented activity.
- A Run has 0..N linear bounded segments but no normative dependency graph. A new Run under the same StepAttempt is a retry only after conclusive pre-boundary non-start; every possibly-started semantic retry is a new StepAttempt pair.
- One **DispatchAttempt** may contain bounded preparation, transport, and response Runs but at most one possible application-level effect-boundary crossing. Its exact state is `ReservedUnsealedV1 | SealedInFlightV1 | TerminalV1(DispatchAttemptTerminalV1)`. It may terminalize seal-free only as `PreSealLocallyRejectedV1`; otherwise exactly one `DispatchCrossingSealV1` moves it to `SealedInFlightV1` before release, permanently consumes the crossing budget, permits only bounded response handling for that exact envelope, and is carried unchanged into terminal `SealedDispatchTerminalV1`. The terminal outcome projection remains exactly `definitely_not_sent | response_received | ambiguous_transport | locally_rejected`.
- One **ReconciliationAttempt** owns exactly one immutable bounded effect-free provider read plan and one fresh authorized Action Request; later polling or plan expansion creates another Attempt.
- One current Step Submission closes the live pair as submitted, appends its Claims, and moves Step open to submitted atomically. Satisfaction remains a separate Gate and authority action.
- Lease expiry and fencing prevent Maestro mutations but do not prove physical termination. A higher-fence takeover requires an exact Takeover Safety Proof or remains blocked.

- One **Candidate Action Manifest** may contain proposed families and leaves from several contexts, but every row has one primary owner and declared cross-context participants. Candidate rows are design evidence only and have no runtime consumer.
- One frozen Action Spec has one closed payload and one fixed atomic publication set. A compound leaf contains no child action list or child Results and exists only for a locked all-or-none invariant.
- One staged external or filesystem protocol owns several separately durable local Action Requests around I/O. Replaying any local request returns its original Result and never reissues the external operation.
- Draft Work creation may produce zero Steps. Tiny Work creation is a distinct atomic compound that also creates the first Step Revision and candidate graph membership; neither action publishes the Contract or acquires execution authority.

- One **Work** has zero or one Work-keyed Design stream; Design remains the stream's semantic owner. A repository-policy **Design Closure Requirement Snapshot** determines whether the Work requires Design or may use one explicit design_root:none exemption.
- One Design stream has exactly one CAS candidate head. Every **Design Revision** has one parent except genesis; stale writers cannot replace the head and their submissions remain recoverable Staging Inputs.
- One Design Revision owns one closed **Design Slot Manifest**. Every required slot is satisfied, explicitly not_applicable under exact authority and Evidence, or missing; appendices can satisfy none.
- Each material candidate Contract Component cites one exact **Design Source Binding**, authorized no-Design source binding, or **Decision Materialization**. The provenance graph is total and typed.
- One **Decision Closure Manifest** covers every Decision owned by the Work and all of its exact Resolutions, supersession edges, consequence classes, Materializations, and effect status. It never filters away superseded-but-effect-live consequences.
- **Design Synthesis** and **Design Reconciliation** are pure Projections over one exact coherent snapshot token. Neither creates or changes Contract Components, Decisions, Work, Steps, planning records, authority, or lifecycle.
- A clean exact snapshot may produce one immutable **Design Finalization Manifest** identity. Content-identical reseal returns that identity; changed input preserves the old record and makes current applicability false.
- One Design Finalization Manifest may have many adapter renderings, but every **Build Handoff** is only a Projection of that same manifest and never competes with Agent Packet for current next action.
- One exact **Build Approval Mandate** binds one Design or explicit no-Design root, complete Decision closure, candidate Contract Root, finalization manifest, scope, exclusions, and stage/proof set. Only the matching initial or amendment Contract-publication transaction may consume it.
- A terminal Work accepts no active Design head advance or new current finalization. Historical migration may preserve Design records without making them current.

##### Projection, Recipe and continuation relationships

- One packet-read request selects exactly one Projection Scope and exactly one of three modes. `BootstrapNoRecipeV1` carries no Recipe request; `DiscoverSelectionContextV1` returns all 30 exact selection options; `ProjectV1` carries exactly one `RecipeSelectionRequestV1`. Its Primary selection has cardinality zero or one from the nine Primary Recipes; its Continuation selection has cardinality zero or one from Bounded Continuation in one of two profiles. Both absent is explicit and omission refuses.
- One `McpPacketReadEnvelopeV1` is exactly `Packet | SelectionContext | NoActiveStore | Unavailable | Stale | Incompatible`. `SelectionContext` has all 30 options and no Frontier or applicability. `NoActiveStore` carries bootstrap facts only for the explicit bootstrap mode. Only `Packet` carries one `PacketRecipeBindingV1`; JobRoute and JobGuidance remain separate Integration values.
- One coherent read validates the exact Release/catalog basis and produces one internal Action Frontier. Projection then seals the corresponding `RecipeApplicationV1` with that Frontier. Every present component evaluates independently against the same Frontier; the request, Frontier and application have no current Head or Receipt.
- Each present component produces `NotApplicable | RestrictiveAdvice | HardStop`; present `NotApplicable` is non-actionable rather than fallback. Their deterministic meet produces one composed Recipe Advice hash. Advice references only Action Specs, WaveRefs, guidance and inspect candidates already admitted by that Frontier.
- A Project request cannot supply more than one Primary. Discovery order never ranks or recommends candidates; any future automatic Primary selection remains a separate fork. Bounded Continuation cannot be Primary, order candidates, select a phase or prefer a Wave.
- Final Projection validates the application and Advice against the same Frontier and independently produces exactly one result: action, complete wave, planning_required, inspect, wait or stop.
- One Agent Packet binds the complete semantic Projection result plus one exact `PacketRecipeBindingV1`: selection-request hash, sealed application by value and canonical hash, ordered zero-to-two component-provenance rows and composed Advice provenance. Every row binds the same Frontier and the Packet hash covers the binding. Its hash is audit closure; it owns no reservation, authority or global write token.
- Each advertised Action Spec binds exactly one subject-scoped Material Dependency Stamp plus its live guards. One Action Request selects exactly one Action Spec.
- One Action Request and Action Result may share one Orchestration Attribution record by value. That attribution has no outgoing authority, Gate, lifecycle, dependency, retry or applicability edge.
- One Capability-owned `JobRecipeEligibilityV1` may reference many exact Recipe identities, but no Recipe Manifest points to a job or Capability Resource. JobRoute is post-Packet Integration material and never an input to RecipeApplication.
- One `JobRouteV1` binds exactly one Release/map/resource resolution basis and exactly one `Packet | Bootstrap` input. A Selected route binds exactly one internal job, one closed reason, one job Resource, zero method Resources and zero Recipes; Ambiguous and Blocked bind no instruction Resource. Only the later Capability-owned `CapabilityMethodResolutionV1` may return an eligible optional method/child/example closure, and that closure is not a JobRoute field or Integration-owned load plan.
- JobRoute has no edge to Recommendation, Operation, Action, Ceremony, authority, applicability, lifecycle, Evidence, Gate, RecipeApplication, Receipt, current Head or persistence. Any Result, read output, mutation, Packet expiry or basis change invalidates it.
- One repository-scoped Projection references many separate Work and Contract subjects without owning them. There is no repository Contract Root or repository acceptance edge.
- One complete wave contains one or more separately authorized and committed members. Different Works are not independent by default, and a ready Work contributes at most one first-acquisition member before reprojection.
- One automation Grant may bound many serial client iterations only within its remaining atomic capacity. Authority owns allocation and consumption; Execution owns Attempts, Runs, dispatch, reconciliation and effect usage; Recipe and clients may only attenuate.
- One external worker has one real Principal and authenticated Session and receives one strictly attenuated Grant path. Worker launch, process count and physical cancellation remain outside Maestro.

- One **Planning Proposal** binds one exact repository Frontier, exact Work and Contract Roots, zero or more exact Observation references, and one or more Scheduling Opportunity references; it owns no canonical fact or outgoing authority edge.
- One Planning Proposal has zero or one winning terminal **Planning Proposal Disposition**. Dispositions are append-only; applicability is derived and concurrent terminal corrections resolve by expected-revision CAS.
- A **Scheduling Opportunity Ref** is exactly one eligible scheduling-participant ActionRef or one complete WaveRef. A Wave and its members cannot multiply one semantic advice claim.
- One repository installation and Repository Store Generation has zero or one current **Scheduling Policy Binding** head and immutable Binding history. One immutable Scheduling Policy Snapshot may be referenced by several historical Bindings but owns no authority.
- The active Repository Governance Floor authorizes Scheduling Policy Binding publication. The core Scheduling Safety Floor may veto policy semantics but cannot authorize them; the candidate policy has no authority relationship.
- One **Scheduling Assessment** binds one exact Scheduling Assessment Input Key and yields ordered equivalence classes, indeterminate, or error. It has no winner, Recommendation, reservation, lifecycle, Gate, or authority edge.
- Planning Proposals, Scheduling Policy Bindings, and Scheduling Assessments may reference Contract, Evidence, Authority, Capability, Resource, Execution, Lease, overlap, and Effect facts by exact identity; those references transfer no ownership or mutation right.
- Final **Projection** derives the expected Scheduling Assessment key, applies core hard stops, validates Recipe Advice only inside the highest admissible equivalence class, and alone emits the Recommendation.
- In Relationships and the Evidence model, unqualified Assessment means Evidence-owned Gate Assessment unless the text explicitly says Scheduling Assessment.

##### Coordination relationships

- One repository owns zero or more immutable Thread Descriptors.
- One Thread Descriptor has exactly one nonempty immutable canonically ordered Coordination Address audience manifest; each member binds one Audience Eligibility Snapshot, and audience change creates another Thread.
- One reachable Thread contains one or more Messages. The first Message and Thread publish atomically; every later Message binds the exact Thread revision and audience hash.

- Handoff references transfer no owned record or authority edge. A recipient continues only through a separately advertised and authorized action.

##### Distribution relationships

- The thirteen inventoried Distribution areas share one closed semantic protocol and zero private mutation, phase, rollback, recovery, or current-ownership engines.
- Candidate or Release Content, Target and Installation Policy, Installed Resource Claim, Distribution Plan, and Distribution Transaction Evidence are distinct roles. Reference among them transfers no semantic-content ownership, physical truth, manager truth, or authority.
- Every Distribution Plan binds exactly one Distribution Authority Domain, one immutable alias-closed target set, exact candidate content, target policy, observed before-state claims, capabilities, ownership evidence, and material-dependency hash. It owns no reservation or mutation edge.
- Every later Distribution Transaction binds one exact accepted same-domain Plan and target set and revalidates every material dependency before each staged effect. Remote acquisition may produce an immutable staged artifact but creates no installed claim, target reservation, apply authority, generic Effect Origin, or local commit.
- A later rollback references exact prior Transaction evidence but is a new same-domain authorized operation against current observed state; intervening user, manager, target, epoch, or transaction change may block it.

- Canonical Store Role is exactly Repository Store or Installation Store. Each exact Distribution Authority Domain has exactly one active domain-bound Store Generation and one sole mutable Maestro publication authority.
- One Repository Store belongs to exactly one Repository Domain. It owns repository canonical truth and has no authority, idempotency, lock, phase, recovery, Projection, or Packet edge into Installation Domain.
- One externally enforceable Installation Realm has zero active Installation Domain before genesis and exactly one afterward. Exactly one Installation Store and one protected active Installation Locator head identify that domain; arbitrary same-realm or per-target Stores are forbidden.
- Several Installation Realms are non-executable until the locator and path protocol proves protected locator-slot, security/mount-realm, and alias-closed target-namespace disjointness. Unresolved discovery, overlap, target swap, or several locators for one Canonical Target Id blocks.
- Repository and Installation Stores are physically and transactionally independent. No request, transaction, idempotency key, lock, authority consumption, Receipt, Result, generation activation, recovery, Projection, Packet, wave, Recommendation, or atomic-success claim spans them.
- The Installation Locator selects one fully verified active Store Generation only after inactive preparation; partial Store, root, locator, Principal, Grant, governance, or namespace artifacts are non-authoritative recovery inputs.
- Store truth is Maestro canonical truth inside its domain only. Filesystem bytes, package-manager state, and remote effects require exact current observations; manager receipts are immutable non-bearer inputs and never authority or current truth.
- Same-realm recovery may retain InstallationId only under external root and monotonic high-water continuity while advancing Store Generation and Authority Epoch. A new realm mints a new InstallationId; ordinary copy never activates; rollback never rewinds Store Generation.
- One legacy combined operation may map to several historical domain dispositions joined only by migration provenance. Correlation transfers no authority, atomicity, current claim, or retry right.
- Topology plus the locked dual-context Authority representation still creates no normal InstallationDomain control plane. Repository governance transition and Projection remain repository-scoped, and normal installation mutation remains unavailable until Installation governance transition, Projection, phase/recovery, and mixed-binary admission close.

##### Authority-context relationships

- AuthorityContextV1 is exactly RepositoryAuthorityContext or InstallationAuthorityContext; one active domain has exactly one active context and any prior contexts are immutable history.
- Each Trust Root Snapshot, Principal Binding, Session, Grant, Delegation, Mandate, Revocation, authorization evaluation, Receipt, quorum contributor, budget and use-consumption record belongs to exactly one Authority Context.

- A non-genesis Grant has exactly one same-context parent and one Delegation. Genesis has zero parents. Every child is a strict subset across every branch-applicable dimension.
- Installation genesis has no live Installation Authority Context before externally verified Locator-head activation. Candidate Trust, Binding, Grant and governance records are inert until that exact visibility point, and the first Session follows activation.
- Repository and Installation authority graphs share one canonical evaluator but no object, path, quorum, budget, consumption, Receipt, idempotency or transaction edge.

- Same-realm recovery may retain InstallationId only through external Trust and authority-high-water continuity while advancing Store Generation and Authority Epoch. New-realm or uncertain continuity creates a new identity and preserves old authority only as audit.

- One live **InstallationAuthorityContext** has exactly one current **Installation Governance Head** and zero or more immutable historical Head revisions; before activated genesis it has none.

- One **Installation Governance Policy Binding** selects exactly one immutable **Installation Governance Policy Snapshot** and belongs to one exact Context, Store Generation, Authority Epoch, Trust Root revision and Governance Head.
- A future ordinary Installation authorization composes exactly one active Floor requirement, one active Policy requirement and one immutable owner-specific requirement; the canonical Authority evaluator alone resolves that conjunction against live context-local Grants and exact Mandates.
- Candidate and migrated governance-shaped material has zero authority until a separately authorized activation selects it; no Plan, manager, adapter, repository Contract or external receipt can become a governance owner.

##### Installation governance-transition relationships

- One same-context Installation governance-content change selects exactly one Policy Binding Replacement or Structural Root/Floor Replacement; the variants are disjoint and root-dominant.
- A Policy Binding Replacement changes behavior-bearing Policy material and no structural Root material. A Structural Root/Floor Replacement changes structural Root material and may also change Policy atomically.

##### Installation governance-comparison relationships

- One current Installation Governance Head and structural Root select exactly one supported Comparison Protocol; candidate governance selects none.
- One usable comparison binds exactly one later-frozen Slot Manifest, one current semantic map and one candidate semantic map inside one Installation Authority Context.

##### Installation governance-certificate value relationships

##### Installation governed-review history relationships

- Pure comparison and Certificate-value derivation produce zero canonical writes.

Absence from complete retained canonical history proves only that neither an Observation nor governed tombstone establishes that fact; it never proves no real-world interaction occurred.

##### Installation governance-review coverage relationships

- Governed Review Publication Coverage contains exactly Direction(Equivalent, Strengthening, Weakening, Incomparable), Invalid, Unsupported, Unsatisfiable and Unknown for every 23fd-constructible Certificate.

##### Governed-review publication establishment relationships

##### Prospective capacity-origin relationships

##### Capacity-origin admission relationships

- One Origin Admission Frame maps to zero accepted v1 kinds until every prerequisite is frozen; it maps to one eligible direction, GovernedCapacitySlot.

## 6. Canonical domain contracts

The canonical normative chain is `Design Resolution -> Decision Materialization -> candidate Contract Root -> exact build approval -> authorized publication -> Contract Generation -> generation-scoped Step Bindings`. Resolution, notes, Messages, Memory and advisor output cannot directly change behavior.

Every mutation is one typed authorized `ActionRequest` selecting exactly one of 145 closed Action leaves, or one disjoint `CeremonyRequest` selecting one of 11 Ceremonies. Unknown, generic, nested, batched, Recipe-defined and adapter-defined operations fail closed. Authority-changing transitions require the Repository or Installation Governance Floor, outgoing requirements and candidate incoming requirements; a candidate policy never authorizes itself.

Every Run has exactly one owner through the closed `ExecutionAttempt = StepAttempt | DispatchAttempt | ReconciliationAttempt` union. StepAttempt binds the exact generation-scoped Step Binding and live Lease fence. DispatchAttempt binds durable Effect Intent and dispatch fence. ReconciliationAttempt binds durable Effect Intent and a fresh authorized Action Request. Dispatch/reconciliation may cite the originating Step Binding only for provenance; it grants no Lease, Evidence applicability, lifecycle authority or Step mutation right.

Every Effect Intent has exactly one stable `EffectIntentHomeV1 = ActiveStoreHomeV1 | NoStoreCeremonyHomeV1 | PreStoreCeremonyHomeV1`, one immutable origination fence, one sole home-local Effect Intent Control Head and a fresh same-home use fence for each later attempt. Active Store is domain-local to Repository or Installation; No Store is only Installation genesis and fabricates no active domain; every other Ceremony effect is Pre Store. Restore may advance Generation/Epoch only after fencing old writers and installing one same-home successor writer term; another domain receives non-bearer history, never a second Control Head or retry right. A locally withdrawable Intent uses exactly one of the ordinary, Bootstrap-G0 or CMA withdrawal branches, is legal only from `None/(prepared | confirmed_not_applied)`, performs one no-I/O Head CAS to `None/cancelled`, and renders `withdrawn locally; no provider cancellation performed`; provider cancellation or compensation remains a fresh separately authorized remediation Intent.

Evidence is immutable source-qualified Observation, Claim and `pass | fail | indeterminate | error` Assessment. Gate satisfaction is derived only from the current applicable `pass` Assessment. Projection computes allowed and recommended next action from exact canonical state; Planning/Recipe may rank only already-allowed actions.

External effects use `Effect Intent -> authorization -> local dispatch fence -> remote or protected attempt -> Observation -> reconciliation`. Possible boundary crossing returns `in_doubt`; fresh reconciliation never revives stale Step authority.

### Supporting detail and retained evidence

The following material is retained from the prior canonical design. It is supporting detail under the synthesis above, not a competing definition; effective supersession and the authority order in Section 1 control.

#### Lifecycle authority

Locked choice: Work owns one universal lifecycle; gates vary requirements; Recipe orchestrates.

The Work bounded context owns one finite, versioned lifecycle graph shared by every Work. Step has a separate bounded execution lifecycle but cannot accept or complete Work.

Policies, profiles, Gates, Recipes, Projections, adapters, readiness flags, metadata, and supporting records may add preconditions or explanations only. They cannot add, rename, reorder, reinterpret, or persist private Work or Step states or transitions. If a legitimate scenario cannot fit the canonical graphs using Gates and typed supporting records, the lifecycle decision must be reopened.

Work remains bounded: high-churn Step attempts, Runs, Evidence payloads, Decision histories, Recipes, and Projections live in their owning records or contexts. Ordinary Step execution does not serialize through Work-wide CAS.

Every mutation passes through one canonical application transition contract. It evaluates a coherent version-stamped snapshot, fails closed on stale, unknown, missing, or partial inputs, then commits state and audit history atomically or through a deterministic recoverable protocol. Gate definitions and evaluations are immutable once referenced and versioned or content-addressed; authorized rebinding creates a new contract generation and invalidates affected evaluations.

Status, readiness, blockers, and next action are pure Projections. Recipe application creates no Recipe Receipt entity; when an advertised action is selected, its Action Request and Action Result may carry immutable non-bearer Orchestration Attribution binding the exact Recipe identity, version, hash and application components. Approval, security, delivery, and release are Gates, never agent-completable Steps. Migration, repair, and override paths require scoped audited authority and expose no generic force bypass.

The exact Work and Step graphs are locked in Canonical state graphs. The profile-to-Gate authoring model is locked in Policy and Gate composition.

Design owns no lifecycle. Design incomplete, reconciled, finalization-current, finalization-stale, and approval-ready are derived Conditions over exact immutable roots, closure rules, Evidence freshness, trusted time, and live authority. Neither finalization nor Handoff changes Work or Step state.

Trusted-time Policy Stack has no independent lifecycle. Candidate values are inert; selection changes only through the owning Authority transition and future 12J success-visible continuity publication. Same-Stack requests do not transition. Historical reselection is a new rotation, not resume, rollback or revival. Planned turnover and recovery remain distinct rows 13 and 15 and cannot reuse the same-context rotation bundle.

Carry Mapping has no lifecycle or current selector. Inert mappings may coexist; pure evaluations die with their exact 70c6 attempt. A later successful transition may retain one non-bearer accepted provenance record only inside the 12J success-visible state. Planned turnover and recovery use distinct branch authority; recovery binds one last-trusted predecessor and zero stale-local authority. Missing carry blocks or routes to separately governed new identity and never repeats genesis.

The external-revision cell has no provider-owned or adapter-owned lifecycle and no latest Head. A fresh Selected incarnation begins Unaccepted. Future 12J may accept Same or Advance status under fresh 12F authority. TerminalVeto is absorbing for that incarnation. Historical Accepted records remain immutable while prospective usability is derived. Rotation, deselection and recovery remain owned by 4c0b and row 15, not by external status.

Continuity Maintenance Authorization has no independent lifecycle or current Head. Its current applicability is derived from the exact success-visible continuity state, G0 classification, job-specific allowed defect, slot state, executor assertion and current basis. Same-lineage phase successors carry exact identity and remaining/spent history. Planned turnover and recovery explicitly map or retire every predecessor slot and prove monotonic high-water. Exhaustion blocks; it never triggers implicit renewal, fallback or recovery.

#### Policy and Gate composition

Locked choice: versioned Policy Profiles compile into an explicit pinned Gate Snapshot.

Profiles exist only to make authoring reusable. Before Work becomes executable, the expansion engine resolves fully qualified profile namespace, origin, exact version, and content hash into canonical Gate definitions and evaluator contracts. The accepted Work contract pins its lifecycle version, contract generation, expansion-engine version, complete profile provenance, resolved Gate Snapshot, and snapshot hash.

All baseline and default requirements are visible in the snapshot. There is no latest selector, inheritance fallback, search-path precedence, or silent local, shipped, and user-global shadowing. Runtime transitions and Projections use only the pinned Gate Snapshot and never consult profile catalogs.

Composition is additive, order-independent, and idempotent. Identical stable Gate identities deduplicate. Non-identical identity collisions, contradictions, cycles, removal or weakening attempts, unknown fields, unknown Gate kinds, and unresolved evaluator contracts fail before execution.

Profiles use an allowlisted declarative schema. They cannot define states, transitions, status aliases, commands, shell or MCP actions, Recipe sequencing, evaluator executables, or side effects. Applying a custom profile requires scoped Work-contract authority and records its source hash and provenance.

Profile or catalog changes never affect existing Work. Re-expansion requires an explicit authorized CAS amendment that appends a new Work contract generation with reason, actor authority, visible before/after Gate diff, and old/new hashes. Affected Gate evaluations are invalidated; historical definitions, snapshots, and receipts remain immutable.

Every Gate evaluation binds the Work generation, Gate Snapshot hash, evaluator contract identity/version/hash, Evidence or Authorization Receipts, freshness inputs, time basis, and result. Evaluators are pure over pinned inputs, cannot mutate Work, and fail closed when unavailable, stale, unknown, or drifted.

Canonical status and next-action Projections show the resolved Gates, per-Gate provenance, satisfaction or blocker state, and relevant versions. Migration preserves this full material and never promotes ambiguous v1 proof.

#### Canonical state graphs

Locked choice: A, minimal explicit lifecycle states plus typed durable records and derived Conditions.

Work lifecycle:

```text
draft -> ready -> active -> awaiting_acceptance -> completed
                      ^              |
                      +-- rejection--+

draft | ready | active | awaiting_acceptance -> cancelled
draft | ready | active | awaiting_acceptance -> superseded(successor)
```

- draft: the intended outcome exists and its contract is still authorable.
- ready: one executable contract generation, lifecycle version, Gate Snapshot, completion authority, and valid acyclic Step graph with at least one required Step are authorized and pinned. Ready does not assert that a Step is Runnable now.
- active: at least one authorized execution action has begun. The first Step Lease action moves ready to active through one atomic or deterministic crash-recoverable operation.
- awaiting_acceptance: one explicit current Work-owned Submission and its immutable finite non-empty `SubmissionClaimSetV1` of Evidence-owned Claims exist; all required current-generation Steps are satisfied and all submission Gates passed at the Submission's exact snapshot.
- completed: scoped completion authority accepted the outcome against one exact coherent current snapshot.
- cancelled: governing intent was withdrawn without replacement.
- superseded: governing intent was replaced before completion by one distinct existing acyclic successor.

Awaiting acceptance returns to active only through an explicit rejected-completion, repair, or material-amendment action with a reasoned immutable receipt. Rejection is not another state. Completed, cancelled, and superseded are terminal. Reopen, undo, or correction never rewrites a terminal Work; it creates a linked successor.

Step lifecycle:

```text
open -> submitted -> satisfied
  ^         |
  +--repair+

open | submitted -> cancelled
open | submitted -> superseded(successor)
```

- open: the current Step revision is not yet under a Step Submission; it may derive as Runnable, leased, running, blocked, stale, or repair-needed.
- submitted: one immutable Step-owned Submission binds the exact Work generation, Step revision, Lease fence and Runs plus one finite non-empty canonical `SubmissionClaimSetV1` of Evidence-owned Claims, and reserves the Step from another Lease.
- satisfied: current Gate assessments and authority accepted that exact Step revision.
- cancelled: execution intent was withdrawn without replacement and an authorized contract amendment removed the Step from the required set.
- superseded: execution intent was replaced by a distinct existing acyclic successor through an authorized contract amendment.

A rejected or explicitly recovered submission appends its result and moves submitted to open; repair uses a new attempt. Satisfied, cancelled, and superseded are terminal. A materially changed satisfied Step remains historical and is replaced by a new open Step; unchanged satisfaction carries only through explicit recorded hash equivalence. Cancellation and supersession never satisfy dependencies or silently rebind edges.

The lifecycle-to-Action map is total and closed under effective efa0:

| Owned lifecycle mutation | Exact primary Action leaf | Fixed atomic participants and boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| create Work as draft | `Work.CreateDraftWork` | Work only |
| Work draft -> ready | `Contract.PublishInitialContract` | Contract publishes; Work advances atomically |
| Work ready -> active | `Execution.AcquireStepExecution` on the first execution | Execution creates the pair; Work advances atomically |
| Work active -> awaiting_acceptance | `Work.SubmitWorkCompletion` | Work publishes its Submission; Evidence publishes the complete Claim set |
| Work awaiting_acceptance -> completed | `Work.CompleteWork` | Work accepts only the exact Submission/Gate snapshot under completion authority |
| Work awaiting_acceptance -> active after rejection | `Work.RejectWorkCompletion` | immutable rejection reason and authority Receipt |
| Work awaiting_acceptance -> active for repair under the current Contract | `Work.ReturnWorkForRepair` | immutable repair directive; no topology mutation |
| Work awaiting_acceptance -> active through material change | `Contract.AmendContract` | candidate Contract publication and affected Work/Step disposition |
| permitted nonterminal Work -> cancelled | `Work.CancelWork` | exact expected lifecycle revision and reason |
| permitted nonterminal Work -> superseded | `Work.AbsorbWork` | successor relation and predecessor transition atomically |
| initialize one generation-scoped Step Binding | `Contract.PublishInitialContract` or `Contract.AmendContract` | exact `OpenFreshV1 | SatisfiedByCarryV1` total initialization |
| Step open -> submitted | `Step.SubmitStep` | Step is primary owner; Execution closes the live pair and Evidence publishes the Claim set atomically |
| Step submitted -> satisfied | `Step.SatisfyStep` | exact Submission/Gate/Assessment/authority snapshot; no live Lease or executor authority |
| Step submitted -> open after rejection | `Step.RejectStepSubmission` | immutable rejection result; prior Submission/Claims remain historical |
| Step submitted -> open through explicit recovery | `Step.RecoverStepSubmission` | distinct recovery authority/reason; prior Submission/Claims remain historical |
| Step open/submitted -> cancelled or superseded | `Contract.AmendContract` | Contract owns topology; Step disposes the Binding atomically |

Reject versus repair or recovery never shares an inner mode: each has a distinct nominal basis, guard set, reason Receipt and atomic publication set. `AbandonStepAttempt` closes only an Execution pair and cannot reject or recover a committed Step Submission. Submit/amend/cancel/supersede, accept/reject/repair/amend, satisfy/reject/recover/amend and submit/renew/takeover races all use exact expected revisions; one writer wins and every loser writes nothing, spends no authority and performs no I/O.

State is intentionally smaller than durable truth. Contract generations, Gate Snapshots, Step revisions and membership, dependencies, Submissions, `SubmissionClaimSetV1` commitments, Claims, Runs, Lease fences, Evidence and freshness, Gate assessments, Authorization Receipts, transition receipts, cancellation and supersession reasons and targets, correction relations, retention receipts, and migration provenance remain typed first-class records. Runnable, leased, running, blocked, stale, repair-needed, failed attempt, progress, next action, and archive visibility are Conditions or Projections only.

Every time-sensitive Projection includes coherent input revisions and hashes, as_of, and valid_until. A cached Projection is disposable, cannot authorize a transition, and cannot be served after valid_until. Lease acquisition or renewal rechecks current readiness, revision, authority, and time, and proves or increments the highest fence. At as_of greater than or equal to expires_at the Lease is expired; an expired or older-fence actor cannot renew, submit, satisfy, or commit Maestro state. External side-effect safety requires the later connector or action contract and is never inferred from a Lease.

A Work amendment appends a contract generation and Gate Snapshot. It invalidates affected assessments and revokes affected Leases or submissions. Satisfaction binds exact Work generation, Step revision, Gate Snapshot, evaluator, Evidence freshness, and authority. Completed Work cannot be amended.

Migration is semantic, not label-to-label. It first classifies whether a v1 artifact owns an independent acceptance boundary and therefore becomes Work, or is subordinate execution and becomes Step. Feature proposed may become Work draft; ready or in_progress may become ready or active only from full contract and execution evidence; closed or shipped becomes completed only with equivalent close authority. Task needs_verification becomes submitted only when the exact Submission subject and every normalized proposition boundary are reconstructible into one finite non-empty canonical Claim set; verified or generic closed becomes satisfied only with equivalent verification. Legacy compound assertions are never guessed apart or merged: ambiguous, orphaned or compound material remains opaque provenance or sealed quarantine and requires revalidation. Rejected or abandoned cannot be flattened without preserving disposition and reason; superseded requires a valid successor. No active v1 Claim synthesizes a live Lease, applicability, satisfaction or authority. Unknown state, ambiguous proof, missing successor, or incomplete authority blocks cutover, stays opaque in the rollback bundle, or requires explicit migration resolution.

The migration consumer inventory includes FeatureStatus, TaskState, generic Card status, Loop phase and status, Proof, QA, Witness, root status, next, ready, and resume, persistence schemas and archives, CLI and JSON, MCP, TUI, hooks, skills, tests, and the TypeScript Mission Control sidecar. Every consumer must use the canonical graph or Projection; none may retain a private lifecycle.

Required later proof includes exhaustive legal and illegal transition properties; lease acquisition, renewal, expiry, and stale-fence races; submitted-claim crash recovery and repair; amendment invalidation and hash-equivalent carry-forward; immutable terminal correction; cancellation and supersession graph safety; archive round-trip identity and history; cross-adapter Projection parity at the same as_of; and migration fixtures for every current status, alias, ambiguous proof, live claim, missing successor, unknown status, interruption, and rollback.

The adversarial review proposed collapsing Work to draft or open and Step to pending or terminal. That refinement is rejected: it would relocate the selected public contract-authorization, execution-start, completion-submission, and acceptance boundaries into supporting-record sub-lifecycles. Its time, fencing, amendment, terminal, dependency, retention, Projection, migration, and proof safeguards are incorporated. Reopen this decision only if a legitimate scenario cannot fit these graphs using Gates and typed records, if the same terminal identity must truly be mutated, or if Maestro is incorrectly required to promise exactly-once external side effects from a local Lease.

The execution subgraph is also locked. One atomic acquisition creates a 1:1 StepLease-StepAttempt pair in live state plus LeaseTerm T1. Renewal appends Tn+1 while the same pair remains live. The pair closes exactly once as submitted, yielded, failed, cancelled, timed_out, lost, or fenced. Submitted moves Step open to submitted in the same transaction; the other pair outcomes leave Step open unless an amendment simultaneously cancels or supersedes it. No terminal pair reopens.

A Run moves reserved to active or to definitely_not_started, cancelled, timed_out, lost, or fenced; active moves to succeeded, failed, cancelled, timed_out, lost, or fenced. Every terminal Run is immutable. Expiry is effective at as_of >= expires_at and is materialized on the next authorized write; time and heartbeat never create a hidden transition worker. Physical execution may outlive every local terminal record, so takeover needs separate safety proof.

#### Evidence model

Locked choice: B, one typed immutable Evidence model with strict bounded-context ownership.

Canonical graph:

```text
Run | human | reviewer | tool | remote receipt
    -> Observation
       subject + revision + producer + procedure
       environment + time + provenance + payload manifest

Work/Step Submission [Work-owned or Step-owned]
    -> SubmissionClaimSetV1 [finite non-empty canonical set]
       -> Claim [Evidence-owned; Observation refs]

Gate node + pinned pure evaluator
    + Observations and/or Authorization Receipts
    -> Assessment
       pass | fail | indeterminate | error

Projection
    -> current Gate satisfaction, conflicts, freshness, blockers, next action
```

Evidence is one logical model, not one physical ledger. Work and Step own Submissions and lifecycle. Gate owns policy and evaluator semantics. Run owns execution and only acquisition procedures intentionally represented as Runs under the closed `ExecutionAttempt` union. Proven-effect-free transport creates no Run; Authority owns acquisition semantics and complete reduction, and Execution owns any effecting DispatchAttempt or ReconciliationAttempt. Authorization owns grants. Projection owns current status and routing. Evidence owns only the immutable typed provenance and assessment graph, payload integrity, invalidation, deterministic export, and bounded retention. It cannot execute commands or reviewers, schedule work, choose Recipes or policy, grant authority, mutate lifecycle, or fetch ambient remote truth.

Observation rules:
- Every Observation has a versioned allowlisted kind and exactly one acquisition or declared derivation event.
- Its manifest binds typed subjects, producer principal and session, procedure, observed and recorded time with clock basis, Work generation or Step revision where applicable, repository and artifact revision, environment and toolchain, provenance lineage, payload descriptors, redaction state, and record hash.
- Identical payload bytes may deduplicate, but Observation identity is never the payload hash. Different producer, time, subject, revision, environment, or procedure means a distinct Observation.
- Unknown Observation kinds remain opaque and cannot satisfy a Gate.
- A URL, job id, object id, note, or agent label is not sufficient Evidence without immutable typed provenance and retained material or a verifiable signed receipt and snapshot.

`SkillActivation` is the closed acquisition-specific application of these rules. Its natural subject includes one fresh acquisition identity, one typed active-Store or bootstrap context, the exact Release and root Skill Resource. Its payload is the complete Selected route, Capability resolution, Recipe resolution, ContextBudgetProfile and loaded Resource closure. The ordinary Observation envelope supplies trusted producer/session/host/procedure/time/environment provenance. Candidate creation is pure; only a separately advertised ordinary-authority `PublishObservation` Action may atomically append the immutable Observation, Result, Receipt and idempotency/acquisition-uniqueness mapping. The publisher validates candidate commitments and current dependency stamps without reopening Resource bodies or rerunning routing. Same-key replay returns the original Result; changed meaning or another key reusing the acquisition identity conflicts. The exact current kind/action/origin catalogs are 43/145/23; efa0 adds no SkillActivation-specific member.

Submission and Claim rules:
- Every submitted Work or Step has exactly one owner-local immutable Submission and one `SubmissionClaimSetV1` commitment binding a finite non-empty canonical set of immutable normalized Evidence-owned Claims. Each Claim binds exactly that one Submission.
- The carrier contains exactly `submission_id`, positive `claim_count` and one ordered array whose entries contain exactly `claim_id`, `normalized_proposition_hash` and `claim_record_hash`. Entries sort lexicographically by canonical normalized-proposition-hash bytes and then canonical Claim-id bytes. Duplicate ids, propositions or record hashes, zero entries, mismatched count, unknown fields, noncanonical order and digest mismatch reject before mutation.
- Its digest is SHA-256 over literal UTF-8 domain `maestro.submission-claim-set.v1`, `submission_id`, unsigned-64-bit big-endian count and every ordered entry, with each variable field encoded as unsigned-64-bit big-endian length followed by exact bytes. The set is bounded only by the shared finite typed-input limit of its Action Request; no second mutable Claim-count limit, ambient default or adapter override exists. The same idempotency key with the same digest returns the original set; changed meaning conflicts.
- A Step Claim binds its Work generation, Step revision, Lease fence, and one or more direct Observations. A Work Claim may additionally bind exact current Step Submissions.
- Claims state propositions only. They cannot declare Gate satisfaction, approval, freshness, independence, or authority.
- A Claim without the Observation class required by its Gate remains submitted but cannot become satisfied or completed.
- The owning Action publishes the Submission, complete Claim set, Result, idempotency mapping and lifecycle transition in one same-Store serializable transaction. Crash before commit exposes none; crash after commit exposes all; stale losers create no orphan record. Committed sets never accept late append, deletion, merge, split, rewrite or reparenting.

Assessment rules:
- Every Assessment binds exactly one Gate node, Gate Snapshot hash, Work generation, optional Step revision, canonical input-set hash, evaluator identity and version, implementation or algorithm hash, parameters, canonicalization and redaction versions, trust-root snapshot, explicit as_of, freshness basis, and valid_until when applicable.
- Empirical leaves consume Observations. Authority leaves consume Authorization Receipts. Mixed leaves keep both classes distinct. Composite Assessments consume child Assessment references only through the pinned acyclic Gate DAG.
- The result enum is pass, fail, indeterminate, or error. Only pass satisfies. Fail is a valid negative conclusion. Missing, stale, unavailable, ambiguous, or conflicting inputs are indeterminate. Evaluator, schema, integrity, or replay failure is error. Indeterminate and error block.
- Equally applicable conflicting Assessments both survive and derive indeterminate with diagnostics. Newest never wins and pass is never preferred. Explicit all, any, quorum, veto, deny-overrides, waiver, and error-propagation semantics must be pinned by the Gate contract.
- One Observation may be assessed for several Gates, but each Gate gets a new Assessment and rechecks every declared binding. Cross-revision or cross-environment carry-forward requires a pinned equivalence evaluator and receipt.

Evidence classes bind enough context for their claim:
- Deterministic command results bind executable bytes and version, arguments, working directory, relevant environment, subject revision and dirty state, exit status, retained output hashes, and start and end time.
- Nondeterministic results bind seed where possible, sample plan, repetitions, thresholds, confidence or error model, and environment. One success is never deterministic proof.
- Manual and visual observations bind actor, procedure, target build, device, viewport, display scale, theme, capture artifact, and time.
- Review observations bind reviewer principal and session, model and tool context, exact review packet and tree hashes, findings, and declared confidence.
- Security observations bind threat scope, scanner and ruleset hashes, dependency or advisory snapshot, exclusions, and target tree.
- Installed-binary observations bind installed path and byte digest to build and commit provenance.
- Delivery and release observations bind target, immutable artifact, tag, and commit digests, publication or deployment receipt, endpoint snapshot, and availability time.

Evaluator and independence rules:
- Evaluators are pure over canonical explicit inputs and as_of. They never invoke commands, agents, networks, ambient filesystem or process state, current time, mutable trust stores, profile catalogs, or latest selectors.
- Humans, agents, tools, and remote systems acquire Observations before evaluation.
- Reviewer output is a Review Observation or Assessment proposal. A pinned evaluator validates subject, packet, findings, identity, independence, freshness, and Gate policy. A worker word such as PASS is not Gate truth.
- Independence is derived from verified principal, session, role, tool boundary, and provenance lineage, not unequal free-form ids. Independent-review Gates reject self-attestation unless the exact producer class is explicitly allowed.
- Historical evaluator definitions and implementation material remain repo-local and content-addressed for offline recomputation.

Authority rules:
- Authorization Receipts remain outside empirical Evidence and bind principal, authentication and authority basis, exact action, subject and revision, reason, conditions, issuance, and expiry.
- Approval, waiver, skip, completion, delivery, and release permission never become Observations.
- A waiver affects only one exact Gate when the pinned policy declares it waivable and accepts that exact scoped receipt. There is no generic force path.

Payload, secrecy, retention, and export:
- Evidence capture minimizes and redacts before persistence. Raw secrets and low-entropy secret hashes are forbidden.
- Large payloads use integrity-checked content-addressed storage separate from manifests.
- Accidental secret capture permits only scoped audited security erasure: append a non-secret receipt and tombstone, destroy the minimum secret-bearing payload or metadata, mark it unavailable, and invalidate all dependent Assessments. This is not ordinary garbage collection.
- Required external material is materialized locally or backed by a verifiable signed receipt plus sufficient immutable snapshot. External loss makes current use indeterminate.
- Retention and garbage collection are policy-pinned, reachability-aware, generation-locked, and audited. Live, rollback, legal-hold, export, and current-Assessment reachability pins payloads. Deletion leaves a tombstone and prevents current reuse.
- Audit export is deterministic and offline-verifiable and closes over manifests, available payloads or tombstones, Submissions, Claims, Gate Snapshots, evaluator material, Authorization Receipts, Assessments, conflicts, invalidations, amendments, migration provenance, retention policy, and a checksummed root manifest.

Concurrency and transition safety:
- Writes use atomic identity allocation, immutable append, idempotency keys, content verification, symlink rejection, and CAS-protected or rebuildable indexes.
- Concurrent conflicting Assessments both survive. A lifecycle transition compares the exact Evidence and Assessment hashes it evaluated.
- Ordinary Observation or Assessment append does not require Work-wide CAS and cannot mutate Work or Step state.

Migration and removals:
- The offline exporter preserves every legacy artifact byte before interpretation.
- Command and test outputs, screenshots, logs, scanner reports, installed-binary checks, delivery receipts, and release receipts may become typed Observations.
- Completion assertions become Claims only when their exact Work generation or Step revision, owning Submission and each normalized proposition boundary are reconstructible; compound or ambiguous source text is preserved without inferred split or merge.
- Legacy verdicts become Assessments only when subject, payload, evaluator semantics, freshness, authority, and independence are reconstructible; otherwise they remain opaque and require revalidation.
- QA baseline definitions become Policy Profiles and Gates; QA slice captures become Observations; witness and advisor findings become Review Observations; skips, waivers, approvals, delivery, and release permission become Authorization Receipts.
- Conflicting verdicts import as indeterminate. Missing external payloads import as unavailable tombstones. Migrated proof is never silently promoted.
- Proof, QA, Witness, and Review are removed as independent stores, lifecycle authorities, and root protocols. Review may remain Recipe or evaluator-role vocabulary; QA may remain profile or Gate vocabulary.
- Consumers to replace include domain proof, Feature verification, Task VerificationBinding and proof receipts, Feature acceptance evidence and sweeps, QA and Witness sidecars, archive gates, Run evidence summaries, status, next, ready, resume, maturity, query, Loop, close, ship, CLI and JSON, MCP, TUI, hooks, schemas, skills, generated references, tests, archives, workbench export, and the TypeScript sidecar.

This model does not introduce Eval, Dataset, Campaign, Score, benchmark scheduling, reviewer orchestration, or a hidden training loop. AI-code evaluation and agent review are ordinary Policy Profiles, Gates, Recipes, Observations, and Assessments inside Work.

Required later proof includes schema and cardinality properties; observation-reuse laundering matrices; deterministic, nondeterministic, manual, visual, review, security, installed-binary, delivery, and release fixtures; offline evaluator replay; four-state and conflict semantics; composite Gate cycles and propagation; self-attestation and forged identity; amendment and invalidation cascades; secret redaction and erasure; retention and garbage-collection races; deterministic export; CAS and idempotency; full migration fixtures; same-snapshot cross-adapter parity; and architecture guards preventing Evidence from owning execution, policy, lifecycle, Projection, network fetch, or scheduling.

Reopen this decision only if a legitimate Gate requires ambient mutable authority or I/O inside evaluation, historical results cannot be recomputed from retained local material, authority cannot remain distinct from empirical Evidence, or Evidence would have to own execution, orchestration, lifecycle, Projection, or scheduling.

Terminology boundary: every unqualified Assessment in this section is an Evidence-owned Gate Assessment with the pass, fail, indeterminate, or error result grammar. Planning-owned Scheduling Assessment is a separate record, may consume exact Observation references as input, and cannot satisfy a Gate, become Evidence, or share a current head or newest-selector rule with Gate Assessments.

##### Trusted-time acquisition Evidence ownership refinement

Decision 1675 replaces only BFDA's unqualified Run owns acquisition sentence. Evidence owns durable Observation provenance, payload integrity, redaction, invalidation, retention and export; it owns no provider choice, plan, slot, effect classification, cutoff, common reference, fault meaning, unit reduction, role realization, time candidate or authority. A durable trusted-time Observation or closure publication is a separate typed authorized mutation and historical only. Pure plan derivation and proven-effect-free transport need no Run; effecting transport and reconciliation keep the existing Execution owners. No Observation, staging byte or commitment can resume a dead challenge or donate to a later attempt.

##### Source continuity Evidence noninterference

Sequence disagreement, gap, rollback, reset, wrap, historical fork, cross-member conflict, empty unit product or world disagreement creates no new Evidence-owned fault and does not alter 1675 E/P. Only material already satisfying 1675 exact pre-seal attributable-fault law can enter E. Row 7 retains protected provenance and returns Unavailable for any later-discovered impossibility. Durable Observations remain separately authorized historical Evidence and cannot reconstruct, persist or donate the ephemeral candidate.

##### Linearization fence Evidence boundary

Row-8 plans, admissions, candidates and normal outcomes are protected attempt-local mechanics, not general reusable Evidence. A carrier-native coverage or nonoccurrence witness may be referenced only by the later owning atomic closure. If authoritative inspection proves occurrence without valid coverage, Evidence owns the durable source-qualified CarrierIntegrityFault Observation; Authority owns the classification rule. Missing row-12 atomic contents are a continuity-closure integrity failure, not silently relabeled as a carrier fault. Ordinary denial and public adapters reveal no protected point, interval, carrier topology or recovery basis.

##### Human enrollment Evidence boundary

External selector assertions, human-presence transcripts, credential-control facts and assurance outcomes enter as source-qualified Staging Inputs or immutable Observations under the closed Evidence model. They authenticate and constrain the exact current G0 action but are non-bearer and do not become a Binding, Grant, Mandate, consent slot or recovery commitment. Consequential presentation and response acquisition, provider effect classification and any owner-specific Effect Origin remain a mandatory row-10 child; 2eb4 creates no hidden external I/O or durable reusable proof pool. Protected failure reveals no subject, selector, commitment or Binding count.

##### Recovery Commitment Evidence boundary

External registration, currentness, veto, assurance and ceremony material enter only as source-qualified Staging Inputs and immutable Observations bound to exact lineage, token, incarnation, policy, challenge, provider and monotonic reference. Evidence authenticates or refutes prerequisites but cannot select a commitment, change local state, create authority or authorize recovery. Missing, stale, equivocal, downgraded or unsupported status is Unavailable. Row 12 owns acceptance and freshness; row 16 owns protected in_doubt diagnosis. No provider response, absence, retry or legacy byte is promoted.

##### Bootstrap interaction Evidence boundary

Evidence owns immutable source-qualified Presentation and Response Observations only. Presentation commits after completed render/handoff; Response commits only after Presentation publication and exact explicit input. Provider bytes, carrier attestations and remote classifications remain Staging Inputs until verified. Observations prove neither perception, comprehension, consent, quorum, authority, target eligibility, provider success nor Mandate. Equal bytes never merge attempts. Crash or ambiguity before commit leaves the real-world event canonically unproven and blocks the consequential path without affecting pure inspection.

##### Bootstrap Mandate Evidence boundary

E138 Presentation and Response Observations prove exact interaction facts only. Issuance accepts only one purpose-specific same-plan affirmative join and separately requires fresh authentication of the same responder Binding; historical Session provenance is preserved but is not current authority. Decline, silence, timeout, ambiguous input, provider success, carrier attestation and presentation-only Evidence create no Mandate. The issuance Receipt is retrospective proof of the committed Action, not permission for the target Action. Evidence retention, invalidation and migration cannot mint or refresh Authority.

##### Consent Slot non-Evidence boundary

A Consent Slot Commitment is deterministic Authority-domain identity, not an Observation, Claim, Assessment, approval fact or bearer. E138 interaction Evidence may later support 8ca2 issuance only after the exact slot parameter is fixed. Neither Evidence, a response, a Receipt nor a historical issuance-binding fact constructs, changes, fulfills or retargets a slot. Migration provenance preserves legacy meaning without promoting it into a slot.

##### Mandate fulfillment Evidence boundary

Presentation, affirmative Response, authentication, assurance and failure-domain Observations may support exact provenance. Evidence cannot define a target, slot, template, assurance policy, eligibility, independence, inventory completeness, selection or authority. Provider success and Receipt presence are never substitutes for the Authority evaluator.

##### Mandate inventory-totality Evidence boundary

Evidence can support faf5 row dispositions but cannot prove the canonical inventory, omit a row, define the census predicate, establish the Store transaction boundary, rank alternatives or authorize a mutation. A count, digest, query receipt or index proof without the authoritative relation derivation is non-bearer metadata.

##### Epoch Root Proposal record Evidence boundary

Evidence may support admission validation or protected Invalidated diagnosis, but it cannot admit a proposal, create a disposition, make a proposal current/applicable, select a successor or authorize activation. Validator output, Receipt and raw proposal bytes are non-bearer until the exact Authority record mutation exists.

AuthorityContinuityManifestCensusProofV1 is a pure non-bearer design-time proof outside the runtime Observation -> Claim -> Assessment Evidence model. It is not permission, currentness, a Receipt or a runtime class. Its oracle independently enumerates owner source inventories and proves equality with dispositions, IncludedBy references, the generated typed sum and descriptors; submitted contributions cannot be the oracle.
ExplicitlyNonContinuity carries exact invariant/proof references but remains design-time classification. A failed invariant reopens design; it does not become a runtime waiver.
For Epoch Root Proposals, an Invalidated fact records a defect proven before activation under the shared serialization basis. A defect found after activation is represented by protected Observation/Claim/Assessment and may support revocation or recovery under fresh authority; it cannot rewrite or append another proposal disposition. Additional causes after a terminal disposition are also Evidence only.

AuthorityContinuityClosureCensusProofV1 is a pure design-time non-bearer proof outside Observation -> Claim -> Assessment. It proves structural totality and grants no authority, currentness, replay right, effect resolution or publication. Protected integrity diagnostics discovered during verification may become Evidence under row 16, but Evidence never repairs an incomplete closure or substitutes a missing class/facet item.

TransitionGuardEvaluationV1 and its refusal are Authority-derived ephemeral calculations, not Observation, Claim, Assessment, Authorization Receipt or proof of external truth. Protected evaluator diagnostics may later become Evidence only under an owning Observation contract; Evidence cannot supply a missing guard term or turn Satisfied into authority.

Decision 83bf adds no Observation or Assessment kind. Stack comparison, guard evaluation and migration classification are pure non-bearer protocol results, not Evidence or authorization. Evidence may later record protected diagnostics or integrity observations under row 16, but those records cannot select a Stack, supply a bridge, satisfy current-owned requirements or authorize rotation.

Evidence owns source-qualified observations and integrity provenance only. Row 12D consumes exact 70c6 candidate commitments without reclassifying source relations or turning Observations into authority. Carry evaluation and disposition totality are pure non-bearer protocol results. A later accepted carry record is Authority provenance, not Evidence, authorization or reusable comparison input.

Evidence owns immutable source-qualified Registration, Status and Anchor Revision Observations, including provider handle and exact operation provenance. Observations grant no currentness, no-veto, veto authority, recovery right or replay. Authority owns the pure exact-basis comparison and accepted cell. A provider Receipt or query silence is never an Assessment or Authorization Receipt.

Evidence owns every durable maintenance Observation and provenance edge, including trusted-time, recovery external-revision, executor-currentness and carrier material. Evidence does not select a CMA, origin, atom, slot, authority basis, allowed defect, spend, currentness or plan continuation. Publishing an Observation is itself a separate slot-spending authorized mutation; the Observation cannot donate its candidate to later acceptance.

##### Effect authorization Evidence boundary

Remote Observations, provider responses, classifications and integrity findings remain Evidence or Execution facts only. They may support a leaf's current applicability or reconciliation evaluator, but never replace ActionAuthorityBasisV1, a CMA slot, executor assertion, Session, Grant or Mandate. Equal bytes and successful provider responses grant no dispatch, reconciliation, retry or currentness.

##### Stack-repair Evidence boundary

Operational-defect and candidate-incoming evaluation may use immutable source-qualified facts, but no candidate-produced trusted-time value, provider result, Observation, Receipt, matching bytes or apparent operational success authorizes repair. Semantic-integrity uncertainty is refusal, not Evidence that the candidate is safer. Historical outage and repair-like legacy records remain provenance only.

A ValidatedTimeCandidate, source Observation, provider response, H_time evaluation or relation is non-bearer and is not durable Evidence of currentness or authority. Evidence may retain source-qualified historical diagnostics only. Authority alone derives the accepted scalar consequence from the exact current basis. A source Gap or other 70c6 relation must receive its row-12H disposition before any companion 12G consequence can publish; H_time magnitude does not erase source uncertainty.

Source responses, counters, provider claims, initial-floor anchors and SourceLaneOriginCandidates remain protected non-bearer inputs or ephemeral evaluations, not accepted Evidence or authority. Only the future 12J-published AcceptedFloor and correlated closure are success-visible continuity facts. Denial, query, audit, crash, stale state and lost races donate no candidate or floor.

Candidate relations, origin candidates, T_forall, Gap requirements and retain proofs are protected non-bearer evaluation inputs, not authority or current floors. The accepted endpoint and Gap companion become continuity facts only in 12J. Gap proves neither fault nor honest-source identity, cannot decrement F or prune worlds, and advances no H_time.

Profile bytes, comparison results, guard Evaluations, anchors, terminal-prefix candidates and provider responses are non-bearer inputs or observations. Remote occurrence remains Execution/Evidence input until 12I-O classifies it; provider success and latest readback never establish Authority currentness.

Authenticated exact-attempt readback is an Observation; Execution owns occurrence classification. Confirmed requires exact unique immediate-successor proof. DefinitelyDidNotOccur requires total absence plus no queued/delayed/partial/latent execution. Unknown and integrity fault remain explicit; provider response, latest state and ordinary not-found never become Authority or currentness.

Pure owner evaluations and guard results are non-bearer inputs. Receipt is retrospective authority provenance, not Evidence or authority. A 5f23 Confirmed occurrence is required evidence for external-backed acceptance but does not itself establish local currentness. Persistence interprets no policy.

Proposal bodies, guard Evaluations, provider responses and Confirmed occurrence witnesses are protected non-bearer inputs. Evidence may prove proposal premises, G0 validity, Mandate eligibility and external occurrence, but grants no preparation or activation authority. Only the c234-published AdmissionFact, exact Mandate consumption, Receipt and Result are success-visible historical facts; they still do not select a proposal or authorize row 13B.

Evidence may prove class membership, current terminal/prospective state, spend/revocation history and effect occurrence, but cannot choose a disposition or authorize activation. The inert plan and its census proof are protected non-bearer candidate material. Terminal facts become success-visible only through 13B/c234; unresolved remote truth remains Execution-owned and cannot be rewritten by the plan.

##### Governed-review provider Evidence refinement

`Evidence.PublishObservation` publishes `GovernedReviewPresentation` or `GovernedReviewResponse` only with that kind's complete subject and payload. Actual render or handoff must be verified before presentation publication; response publication requires an explicit response joined to the exact committed presentation. Silence produces no response. Observations remain immutable non-bearers and cannot issue, satisfy or consume a Mandate or create a disposition.

##### Distribution acquisition Evidence refinement

A determinate authenticated provider result is published through `Evidence.PublishObservation` as `RemoteReadback`. Provider response, receipt, cache, digest or signature presence alone is not trusted-candidate proof; pinned digest, signature, schema and trust checks may produce a separate Assessment. `DistributionFilesystemState`, `DistributionInstalledResource` and `DistributionManagerState` remain reserved for later local phases and cannot substitute for remote readback.

##### Capability-probe Evidence refinement

`Evidence.PublishObservation(CapabilityProbe)` records only observed availability or effect readiness for one complete `CapabilityProbeSubjectV1`. Provider denial is source-qualified provider output, not Maestro Authority denial. Ambiguous remote state publishes no available/unavailable/ready assertion. Process liveness, security analysis, installed binary and remote readback use their own existing kinds. No Maturity Observation exists.

##### CMA Observation compatibility closure

The exact whitelist is: TrustedTimeAcquisition to TrustedTimeAtomicUnit or TrustedTimeAcquisition; RecoveryExternalRegistration to RecoveryExternalRegistration or registration-routed RecoveryExternalAnchorRevision; RecoveryExternalStatus to RecoveryExternalStatus or status-routed RecoveryExternalAnchorRevision; MaintenanceExecutorCurrentness to MaintenanceExecutorCurrentness; and ProspectiveContinuityCarrier to ProspectiveContinuityCarrier, ExternalHighWaterReadback or CarrierIntegrityFault. Every other purpose/kind pair is unavailable. An Observation is immutable and non-bearer and cannot satisfy the executor assertion that authorizes its own acquisition or publication.

##### Basis-qualified Evidence publication refinement

Evidence now has seven Action leaves: the prior four, two G0-only Bootstrap presentation/response publications and one CMA-only continuity-maintenance publication. The Action validates the exact source and mutates only its own local publication/slot-spend successor. The emitted Observation remains immutable and non-bearer and cannot authorize, advance continuity, satisfy a Gate, issue a Mandate, retry or grant currentness. Ordinary `PublishObservation` structurally rejects Bootstrap and CMA subjects.

#### Agent control plane

Locked choice: B, one bounded Agent Packet plus typed Action Request and Action Result contracts.

```text
Canonical records
      |
      v
Projection -> bounded Agent Packet
                    |
       actor selects one advertised Action Spec
                    v
              Action Request
                    |
       canonical handler rereads records
                    v
 Action Result + receipts + next Agent Packet
```

Agent Packet is a versioned view, never a mutation capability. It binds schema version, packet identity, complete semantic audit hash, as_of, valid_until, visibility and authority view, one closed Work-or-repository scope manifest, the separate Work, Contract Root, Step, Gate, relation, capability, scheduling and resource facts material to the result, one result-shaped Recommendation, the closed advertised Action Specs, required inputs, authority and side-effect classes, idempotency and retry guidance, completeness bounds, and bounded inspect references. Repository scope creates no synthetic aggregate. Packet hash is audit and parity provenance, not global CAS; every Action Spec carries its own complete positive-and-negative Material Dependency Stamp and live guards.

Routine packets have strict byte, row, depth, and provenance budgets. They must be complete for every claim they make. Active stops, guards, required authority, and parallel-wave membership are never truncated. If safe completeness exceeds a bound, the packet reports incomplete or blocked and exposes only exact typed inspection actions; it never guesses one next action from a partial view. One recommendation may name one action or one explicit independent wave. Other allowed actions remain visible only within the same bound.

At a frozen runtime version, Action Spec kinds form a closed exhaustive two-level application-action algebra.
