For one already accepted H_time and one already validated closed proof interval [lower, upper] on one exact Authority Selection Basis:

~~~text
missing, malformed, incompatible, nonfinite, lower > upper -> Unavailable
upper < H_time                                             -> TimeUnavailable
effective_lower = max(H_time, lower)

upper < not_before                                        -> Premature
not_before <= effective_lower and upper < not_after       -> Live
effective_lower >= not_after                              -> ExpiryCertain
otherwise                                                 -> TimeUnavailable
~~~

H_time is the monotonic proven-lower-bound time component of the later closed continuity high-water for one stable Authority lineage and pinned coordinate plus source-policy basis. #### Work relation algebra

Locked choice: B, a closed two-plane algebra separating contract-owned cross-Work prerequisites from immutable lineage.

```text
Contract-owned normative prerequisite:

W-release@H3
  requires completed(W-build@H7)
  scope: before_step(release@R4)
          |
          v
built-in Requirement Gate -> derived blocked/runnable

Immutable canonical lineage:

W-old --superseded_by--> W-new
W-fix ------corrects---> W-old
W-follow ---continues--> W-old
W-a -------references--> W-b

Step dependency = inside one Work only
blocks = Projection only
```

##### Normative prerequisite plane

A Work Requirement is a normalized Contract Component inside the consumer Contract Root. Its identity includes schema version and stable relation id; its content pins one same-repository target Work id, one exact published target Contract Root, the closed predicate target Work completed at that root, and one enforcement scope.

The scope grammar is closed:

- before execution: no Step in the consumer Work derives Runnable or may acquire a Lease until satisfied;
- before Step: one exact consumer Step id and revision is blocked, with downstream effects following the ordinary intra-Work Step DAG; or
- before completion: execution may proceed, but completion submission and acceptance cannot pass until satisfied.

A Work may be draft, publish its contract, and become ready while its Requirements are unsatisfied because ready means contract-authorized, not currently Runnable. The current Projection exposes each exact Requirement and its satisfaction or indeterminate reason. Multiple Requirements are conjunctive. OR and quorum are allowed only through explicit typed Gate Snapshot composition over distinct Requirement Gate leaves.

The Work Requirement is the only cross-Work topology authority. A built-in pure Requirement Gate references the component hash and evaluates target Work id, exact target root, completed lifecycle state, Store Generation, invalidation state, and as_of from one coherent Canonical Store snapshot. There is no free-form completed-Work Gate, generic depends-on record, stored inverse blocks edge, or adapter-specific readiness check. Step DAG edges remain strictly intra-Work.

Candidate Contract publication rejects a self edge, unresolved or unpublished target root, duplicate conflict, or cycle across the active Work Requirement graph plus the candidate. Identical Requirements deduplicate. A target may be incomplete when referenced, but must already exist with the exact published root. Completion later changes only derived satisfaction and runnable or completion Conditions.

Target amendment, cancellation, supersession, missing data, corruption, retention failure, or restore mismatch never follows a successor or newest root. The Requirement becomes unsatisfied or indeterminate with a typed reason. The consumer must publish an authorized amendment or provide a purpose-specific Equivalence Receipt over the exact old and new target roots for this Requirement. Satisfaction transfers no target Claim, Observation, Assessment, Gate pass, authority, state, completion, acceptance, Step, or payload. Reuse of target Evidence remains an explicit Assessment input under ordinary provenance, freshness, and equivalence rules.

Direct cross-repository Work Requirements are forbidden because independent stores cannot supply one coherent transactional snapshot. External prerequisite material is retained locally as a signed Observation under pinned trust, freshness, and Gate evaluators. It becomes a Claim only through one explicit local Work- or Step-owned Submission and that Submission's atomic `SubmissionClaimSetV1` publication; a foreign signed assertion never imports directly as a Claim, never becomes an orphan Claim, and grants no satisfaction or authority.

##### Lineage and reference plane

Lineage records are canonical immutable records outside both endpoint Contract Roots. Every record binds repository identity, exact endpoint Work ids and observed roots or revisions, canonical direction, relation schema version, immutable reason and provenance, expected revisions, and idempotency key. Candidate hashes exclude their future Authorization Receipt. The canonical action evaluates authority over every mutated endpoint and joins the committed relation, any lifecycle history, retrospective Receipt, and Action Result atomically.

SupersededBy is stored predecessor to successor. The predecessor has outdegree zero or one and exactly one when its lifecycle state is superseded; one successor may replace several predecessors. Endpoints are distinct and the graph is acyclic. Creation is one transaction with the predecessor transition to superseded(successor), its reason, expected revisions, uniqueness constraint, and receipt linkage. Concurrent superseders cannot both win. The inverse supersedes view is derived.

Corrects is stored correction Work to a completed target Work. Continues is stored new Work to a completed or cancelled predecessor. Each edge has one target; each Work may participate in zero or more edges. Both graphs reject self edges and cycles. Neither relation mutates the target, designates canonical latest, cascades acceptance or cancellation, inherits authority, rebinds dependents, or carries Evidence, Assessment, Gate satisfaction, or completion. If a correction proves old material wrong, separate typed Evidence invalidations and authorized amendments or successor Work express the impact. Completed history remains immutable.

Work Reference is directional, strictly informational, permits cycles, and rejects self edges. It may appear only in bounded inspection and navigation. No lifecycle, Gate, authority, Recipe, safety, retention, readiness, or next-action rule may read it. A relationship that affects behavior has crossed the materiality boundary and must be represented by a Work Requirement, another Contract Component, a closed lineage action, Gate, or Evidence record.

There is no parent-child Work relation. Subordinate executable work is Step. An independently accepted outcome is another Work and uses exact Requirement or lineage semantics if a real relationship exists. Grouping without domain behavior is a Projection or presentation concern and cannot create ownership, acceptance, cancellation, completion, retention, visibility, or authority inheritance.

A physical relation table may unify storage, but only typed domain actions write it and each kind retains closed database constraints. No public or adapter API accepts an arbitrary kind, predicate, callback, lifecycle effect, projection effect, or metadata map.

##### Work-relation migration, proof, and reopen boundary

Migration semantically classifies every v1 dependency, blocker, Progress order, parent, child, link, successor, inbox coordination edge, and related reference. A child without its own acceptance boundary becomes Step. Independently accepted records become Work. A normative Work Requirement or lineage relation imports only when endpoint identities, direction, exact roots, predicate, enforcement point, lifecycle effect, cardinality, and authority are reconstructable. Generic non-behavioral links may become Work References. Ambiguous or unknown material remains in the lossless rollback bundle, blocks cutover, or requires explicit migration resolution; it never receives normative meaning by guess.

Required proof includes kind and cardinality constraints; self-edge and cycle properties; candidate publication against concurrent graph change; all three enforcement scopes; coherent target completion and amendment races; exact Equivalence Receipt carry; cancelled, superseded, missing, retained, corrupt, restored, and migrated targets; no state, Evidence, or authority transfer; explicit correction impact; concurrent supersession uniqueness; reference noninterference; cross-repository refusal; rejection of a foreign signed assertion imported directly as a Claim or without one local atomic `SubmissionClaimSetV1`; same-snapshot CLI, JSON, MCP, TUI, hook, skill, Packet, and Projection parity; sealed export and restore graph equality; and fixtures for every current dependency, blocker, parent-child, link, successor, ambiguous direction, and missing target.

Reopen only if a legitimate prerequisite cannot use completed-at-exact-root with before-execution, before-Step, or before-completion scope; correct execution requires a coherent live cross-repository relation; one predecessor must have several canonical supersession successors; correction must retroactively rewrite terminal Work instead of explicit invalidation and successor Work; or a new relation kind has unavoidable lifecycle meaning that cannot be represented as a Contract Component, Gate, Evidence record, or closed lineage relation.

#### Authority policy transitions

The canonical transition law is:

```text
EffectiveTransitionRequirement =
    RepositoryGovernanceFloor
    AND CurrentOutgoingTransitionRequirement
    AND CandidateIncomingActivationRequirement
```

This is logical conjunction over the closed authority grammar. It is never permission union, a stricter-wins heuristic, or permission to choose the easiest branch. Equivalent clauses deduplicate without weakening any obligation.

The active Store Generation, Authority Epoch, and Trust Root context pin an immutable versioned Repository Governance Floor. The floor contains a small non-bypassable Authority Transition Protocol and minimum assurance constraints, not mutable hidden policy or actual Principals. Every executable Contract Root includes closed outgoing and incoming transition requirement snapshots, so current and candidate roles are explicit and content-addressed without hashing the runtime actors or Receipts that will authorize publication.

Before publication, a pinned classifier compares the exact current and candidate snapshots across the full closed grammar:

- **Equivalent**: semantically identical clauses deduplicate, and floor, current, and candidate still pass.
- **Strengthening**: floor, current, and candidate all pass.
- **Weakening**: all three pass and one exact nondelegable one-use human downgrade Mandate is consumed.
- **Incomparable**: all three pass and the same exact downgrade Mandate is consumed.
- **Invalid, unknown, unsatisfiable, or contradictory**: publication fails closed; an explicitly staged intermediate transition is required.

Conjunction is field-safe. Assurance takes the stronger value. Subject, action, and connector allowlists intersect. Budgets, use counts, effect ceilings, validity windows, and delegation depth take the narrower bound. Prohibitions union. Every quorum and independence clause remains independently satisfied. No contributor, partial Grant path, or one-shot Mandate may be counted twice to manufacture quorum or independence.

A downgrade Mandate binds the exact repository, Work, current Contract Root, candidate Contract Root, semantic-diff hash, authority-policy transition action, authenticated human, carrier, nonce, expiry, and maximum one use, with no delegation. Candidate-scoped Grants may be established before activation to make a legitimate handoff possible, but they do not make candidate policy live. Actual Principals, Grants, Mandates, Revocations, Receipts, and credential material remain outside candidate hashes.

First Work publication has no current Work requirement and therefore satisfies the active Repository Governance Floor plus the candidate incoming requirement. Repository genesis is the sole explicit human-present bootstrap ceremony before a candidate or floor exists. A floor or Trust Root rotation satisfies the current floor, proposed floor, and a predeclared continuity or root-rotation rule; any weakening additionally consumes exact downgrade consent.

Recovery is not force. It satisfies the last trusted predeclared recovery requirement, destination floor, and exact break-glass Mandate while holding the exclusive generation lock and advancing Authority Epoch. Prospective authority is suspended during recovery. If the current store is unreadable, recovery uses a sealed last-trusted recovery snapshot or fails closed. Migration similarly satisfies the repository floor, candidate incoming requirement, and an exact migration Mandate; legacy actors, roles, approvals, and prose never become live authority by inference.

One SQLite transaction locks the expected Store Generation, Contract Generation, Authority Epoch, and transition inputs; re-evaluates floor, current, candidate, live Grants and Mandates, semantic classification, revocation, time, budgets, uses, quorum, and independence; consumes any one-shot Mandate; then publishes the new generation, retrospective Receipt, Action Result, and idempotency result atomically. A revocation, expiry, concurrent amendment, Trust Root rotation, or competing consumption causes conflict or rejection with no partial activation.

Required proof includes deterministic classification across the full grammar; downgrade, quorum, independence, scope, budget, connector, and no-laundering attack matrices; candidate-scoped Grant preactivation; Mandate binding, replay, and double-spend tests; revocation, expiry, amendment, Trust Root, and publication races; unsatisfiable-candidate diagnostics; first-publication, genesis, migration, restore, recovery, and epoch fixtures; no-self-reference checks; and adapter parity plus sealed-export replay. Reopen this decision only if the closed grammar cannot classify weakening, a legitimate handoff cannot pre-establish candidate authority, dual evaluation creates an unavoidable lockout without a generic bypass, the protocol cannot remain a small Trust Root invariant, or recovery continuity cannot be represented without self-authorization.

#### Decision lifecycle and normative effect

Decision is supporting governance history, not a second Contract, lifecycle, or authority store. It answers what exact fork was presented, what immutable alternative was selected, why other alternatives lost, who authorized that exact selection, and which later Contract change, if any, materialized it.

The canonical records are Decision, Decision Revision, Alternative, Resolution, Decision Supersession, Decision Materialization, and Decision Batch Receipt. A Decision belongs to exactly one Work. It has 1..N immutable revisions and one CAS head while open. Each revision binds the exact question, subject and base hashes, and 2..N mutually exclusive Alternatives. Every Alternative declares immutable meaning, preview, and either no_contract_effect or a closed typed consequence-plan hash relative to the exact base Contract Root.

The lifecycle is:

```text
open --append Decision Revision--> open
open --resolve exact Alternative-> resolved
open --withdraw with reason------> withdrawn
resolved --resolved successor----> superseded
```

There is no reopen, unlock, or in-place semantic edit. Editing an open question or option appends a revision and makes every Mandate for the prior revision stale. Clarification after resolution may append non-normative annotation; changed meaning requires one atomically resolved successor and an immutable acyclic Decision Supersession record. Split or merge repair creates separate new Decisions rather than pretending one-for-one supersession.

A Resolution selects exactly one Alternative and binds the Decision and revision hashes, exact option and consequence hashes, subject and base hashes, rationale, rejected-option reasons, authority requirement, and Authorization Receipt. The consumed human Mandate binds the exact prompt-to-option mapping, authenticated human, carrier, nonce, expiry, and maximum one use. Raw chat, an option letter, advisor output, Session identity, source-approval prose, and actor labels are provenance only unless a trusted interaction envelope establishes that binding.

Resolution has no direct normative effect. Lifecycle, Gate, Recipe, Step-runnability, and Projection code are forbidden from consulting Decision records. A separately authorized Decision Materialization interprets only the selected closed consequence plan against the exact base root, produces exact changed Contract Component hashes and a candidate Contract Root, and records the immutable join among Resolution, before and candidate roots, invalidation or Equivalence Receipts, and the amendment Action Request. Canonical authority-policy transition and Contract publication then decide whether the candidate becomes executable.

Stale-base materialization rejects. A purpose-specific Equivalence Receipt may prove that the selected consequence remains applicable, but there is no silent rebase or newest-root interpretation. One Resolution may have 0..N materializations over history; one Contract Generation may materialize 0..N Resolutions. If the consequence is already satisfied, materialization records an exact equality or equivalence-backed no-op without minting a gratuitous generation.

Effect status is derived rather than written: unapplied, applied to exact root, historical, stale, or superseded-but-effect-live. Decision Supersession never rolls back an active Contract Root, retargets dependencies, changes Work state, carries authority or Evidence, or mutates existing materializations. Any changed normative effect requires a new materialization and publication.

Independent forks remain separate Decisions. One Decision never multi-selects unless the indivisible combination is itself one explicit Alternative. Other requires a new Alternative and Decision Revision before selection. A lock-all interaction is an all-or-none non-nesting batch of 2..N exact child Resolutions. Its Mandate enumerates every Decision Revision and selected Alternative hash. Decision Batch Receipt is an audit envelope only and has no set-level ruling, lifecycle, or supersession.

A terminal Work accepts no new Decisions, supersessions, or materializations. A correction or continuation Work is the exact subject of any later governance fork; Decision remains the semantic owner of its question, options and Resolution. An optional atomic resolve_and_publish Action Spec is only an adapter convenience: its one Mandate must explicitly bind both the exact selection and complete candidate-root diff, and the transaction independently satisfies every Resolution, materialization, authority-transition, and publication invariant.

Migration preserves every v1 byte, identifier, timestamp, context, ruling, rejected option, preview, lineage field, DecisionSet snapshot, approval or advisor text, override, note, store provenance, and original ordering. A canonical Resolution is created only when owning Work, question, complete Alternative set, exact selection, subject and base closure, lineage, and fresh vNext authority are reconstructable. Otherwise the input becomes an opaque Legacy Decision Artifact with no normative effect. DecisionSet children migrate individually; the set becomes only a batch audit artifact. Compressed summaries, global or orphan records, ambiguous choices, missing options, invalid multi-edge or cyclic lineage, and unauthorizable locks remain lossless history and block any claimed active effect rather than being guessed into vNext semantics. Handoff freshness never implies materialization.

Required proof includes canonical hash stability, unknown-field rejection, option uniqueness, all cardinalities, stale revision and prompt mapping, wrong option or carrier, nonce replay, expiry, revocation, and double-spend rejection; Resolution, withdrawal, annotation, and supersession noninterference with Contract and runtime state; exact and stale materialization, equivalence no-op, invalidation, combined-decision conflict, and atomic compound-action cases; concurrent resolution, revision, supersession, amendment, and idempotency races; batch all-or-none and per-child authority audit; terminal Work rejection; and complete fixtures across current file, SQLite, frozen Markdown, DecisionSet, compressed, dangling, cyclic, multi-edge, global, orphan, and missing-authority records. Sealed export and restore must deterministically answer what was asked, what options were shown, who authorized which exact choice, what Contract changed, and what remains executable.

Reopen this decision only if runtime legitimately must consult Decision instead of Contract material; one-fork and one-selection cannot represent a real indivisible choice; safe supersession requires active split or merge semantics; explicit materialization cannot close the governance-to-runtime boundary even with a compound action; or lossless migration cannot preserve legacy history without promoting unverified rulings.

The compatibility sunset is explicit. Current v1 handoff fingerprinting, accept gating, and prepare gating may consume Decision prose only as a legacy transition check while v1 remains the active runtime; no vNext executable state, Gate, Projection, Packet, or publication derives from that fingerprint. Migration inventories raw file, database, archive, frozen-Markdown, duplicate, shadowed, and unreadable sources before any normalized scan, preserving byte sequence, locator, container order, parse failure, and provenance because current typed round trips are not byte-preserving and tolerant scans may omit records. Historical per-card CAS, sequential supersession, and compensating DecisionSet rollback never prove aggregate atomicity. Even the v1 Decisions that established this vNext design require fresh vNext reconstruction and authority before becoming canonical Resolutions; they cannot bootstrap themselves.

Design closure never computes a filtered effective Decision list. The canonical vNext Decision Closure Manifest enumerates every Work-owned Decision head and exact revision, terminal status, Resolution, both raw supersession directions, the normalized one-for-one successor edge or explicit invalid-lineage disposition, consequence classification, every N:M Materialization, and derived effect status. Raw `supersedes` and `superseded_by` disagreement, a unilateral edge, multi-edge, cycle, or merge claim is retained byte-exactly as legacy provenance and cannot silently become a canonical vNext edge. The current v1 feature records are external design-authority inputs, not instances of that future canonical model: their separate external closure may recognize a matched N:1 composite-incorporation head solely to determine which locked design text the packet binds, but Stage 0 reconstructs each consequence separately and imports no composite Decision Supersession. An explicit no_contract_effect closes rationale-only decisions. Open material choices, unresolved conflicts, stale or incomplete materializations, behavior-bearing Resolutions not wholly accounted for in the candidate root, and missing superseded-but-effect-live coverage block finalization.

#### Step DAG and amendment transition

Every published executable Work Contract contains one complete immutable content-addressed Step Graph Snapshot. A stable Step id belongs to exactly one Work and has 1..N immutable Step Revisions. A graph node is not a mutable Step row: it is a generation-scoped Step Binding identified by repository, Work, Contract Root, Step id, and Step Revision hash. Step lifecycle, Step Lease, StepAttempt, Submission, satisfaction, and current Step applicability attach to that binding. Every Run instead has exactly one owner through the closed typed ExecutionAttempt union; dispatch and reconciliation may cite this binding only as provenance.

A Step Revision closes over the outcome and Claim schema, inputs and outputs, action and effect scope, resource and budget requirements, Step-scoped Gate references, authority requirement references, environment and target constraints, and every other value that can change allowed execution or valid completion. One Step id appears at most once in a graph snapshot. One exact revision may appear in several generations of the same Work, but each appearance is a distinct generation binding.

A published graph has 1..N required nodes. Each edge joins exact bindings inside the same Work and snapshot and means that the dependent requires the exact predecessor binding satisfied or covered by an exact purpose-specific carry receipt. Self edges, duplicate nodes or edges, dangling or stale revision endpoints, cross-Work endpoints, cycles, unknown fields, and incomplete closure fail closed. Waves, lanes, preferred order, resource serialization, and optional orchestration belong to Recipe or Projection policy and never become hidden DAG semantics.

An amendment candidate always provides a complete graph snapshot, never an executable patch. A deterministic transition planner compares the exact current and candidate roots and partitions every old node exactly once as retain_exact, replace, or remove and every new node exactly once as retain_exact, replacement, or add. The two snapshots are authority; the Amendment Disposition, impact closure, invalidation plan, and carry proposals are transition evidence outside the candidate hash.

Retention and replacement are one-to-one. Split or merge changes are represented as remove plus add and infer no state, satisfaction, Evidence, authority, or dependency transfer. Added and materially replaced bindings start open. An old open or submitted binding replaced one-to-one becomes superseded by the new binding. An old open or submitted binding removed without successor is cancelled by the amendment receipt. Satisfied, cancelled, and superseded bindings remain terminal history; a changed satisfied binding stays satisfied historically while its replacement opens separately. Leaving current graph membership never rewrites historical state.

`retain_exact` is total through `RetainExactInitializationV1 = OpenFreshV1 | SatisfiedByCarryV1`. The new distinct binding commits `open` when the old binding is `open`, `submitted`, `cancelled`, or `superseded`, and when the old binding is `satisfied` without a valid Step-satisfaction-equivalence carry. It commits `satisfied` only when the old binding is `satisfied` and exactly one valid purpose-specific satisfaction carry is included in the same authorized publication. No retained binding initializes `submitted`, `cancelled`, or `superseded`.

`SatisfiedByCarryV1` is atomic initialization, not a fabricated Submission, transferred Claim, or observable `open -> satisfied` runtime transition. Its non-bearer receipt binds the exact old/new bindings and roots, old authorized satisfaction basis, Step revision, incoming dependency closure, Gate Snapshot/evaluator, every material context value, equivalence purpose, publication authority and resulting state. Invalid, stale, wrong-purpose, wrong-subject, incomplete, duplicate or conflicting supplied carry rejects the whole publication; omission deterministically selects `OpenFreshV1`. Observation-, Gate-Assessment- and authority-applicability carries never change lifecycle. Execution equivalence never changes lifecycle and may create a linked higher-fence pair only under fresh current execution authority. Old lifecycle records remain byte-identical history.

Publishing a new Contract Root invalidates every old Agent Packet, Action Request, Lease mutation token, renewal, Submission, satisfaction request, and current-state commit. No live Step Lease, StepAttempt, Step-execution Run, Submission, or satisfaction transfers automatically, even when the Step Revision hash is retained exactly. DispatchAttempt and ReconciliationAttempt history remains with its durable Effect Intent and gains no current-root authority from an origin-binding reference. Fence high-water is monotonic across a Step history. An old-root process may continue physically and emit attributable historical Observations, but its old token can never renew, submit, satisfy, or mutate current state.

Current execution continuation is explicit. A pinned evaluator proves execution equivalence across the exact Step definition, incoming dependency closure, Gates, authority, effects, inputs, environment, target, resources, and relevant Contract material. The old Lease closes, current execution authority is re-evaluated, and a linked higher-fence Step Lease plus continuation StepAttempt binds the new root. If any input is unknown or authority is absent, the new binding is merely runnable for later acquisition. Amendment authority never grants execution authority. A stale Attempt result may affect current state only through separately authorized reconciliation and applicability evaluation.

Observations are immutable and never erased by amendment. Claims, Submissions, Assessments, satisfaction applicability, and authority applicability remain bound to their original root. Invalidation is append-only and names the changed component plus affected downstream closure. Carry is divided by purpose: execution equivalence, Step-satisfaction equivalence, Observation applicability, Gate-Assessment applicability, and authority applicability. No blanket unchanged or transitive-equivalence receipt exists. A changed incoming predecessor or other material context invalidates downstream applicability even if command or payload bytes match, unless the pinned purpose-specific evaluator proves the exact consumed subject equivalent.

Ready Work remains ready and active Work remains active after a valid amendment. Any material amendment while awaiting_acceptance atomically invalidates the completion Submission and returns Work to active. Terminal Work cannot amend. Amendment publication never implicitly acquires a Lease, submits or satisfies a Step, submits Work completion, or accepts Work.

Candidate objects and the deterministic transition plan may be staged outside authority. One short SQLite transaction rechecks expected Store Generation, Work lifecycle revision, current Contract Root and graph hash, Authority Epoch and revocation head, exact Step Bindings, Lease fences, Submissions, completion state, publication authority, and idempotency key. It then publishes the new generation and graph reachability, binding lineage and disposition, Step and Work transitions, higher fences, invalidations, carry receipts, Authorization Receipt, and Action Result atomically. A fault exposes either complete old state or complete new state, never a partial graph.

Lease acquisition or renewal, Step Submission or satisfaction, completion Submission, acceptance, another amendment, and publication all serialize through the same expected revisions. One wins; the loser is stale with no partial state or consumed Mandate. A self-removing amendment action commits its publication and Action Result against the old pre-state while fencing its initiating Step Lease in that same transaction, so it cannot submit afterward. If an external effect is dispatched or in doubt, its Effect Intent survives graph removal. Publication or completion blocks unless the effect is proven unaffected or the candidate carries explicit reconciliation or compensation handling; Step removal is never permission for blind retry.

Migration inventories every mutable v1 Task, Progress row, dependency, wave, lane, order, gate flag, gate kind, blocker, acceptance, claim, verification binding, assignment, and current_task marker before interpretation. It reconstructs and validates a complete graph per resulting Work. Cross-acceptance-boundary dependencies become exact Work Requirements or block as ambiguous. Gate-like Tasks become Gates. Human, external, and Decision blockers become typed policy or unresolved migration material. No claimed_by, claimed_at, in_progress status, current_task marker, or historical ownership synthesizes a live Lease. NeedsVerification or Verified becomes a current Submission or satisfaction only when the exact owner, subject, generation, Evidence, authority and complete finite non-empty proposition set are reconstructable and freshly evaluated. The importer computes the canonical `SubmissionClaimSetV1` order and digest only from those proven records; it never infers a split, merge or missing Claim. Ambiguous rows remain lossless non-normative artifacts or block cutover.

Required proof includes closed ExecutionAttempt exhaustiveness, exactly-one Run ownership, provenance non-authority, Step Lease versus dispatch-fence isolation, fresh reconciliation authority, and deterministic Step Revision, graph, disposition, impact-closure, and Contract-root bytes; graph closure, cardinality, cycle, duplicate, and unknown-field properties; one- and many-Claim `SubmissionClaimSetV1` golden vectors over its exact fields, unsigned-64-bit big-endian count and length-prefixed field framing, domain-separated digest equality, canonical ordering, zero/duplicate/orphan/cross-Submission and malformed-set refusal, the one shared Action Request typed-input bound with no second count limit/default/adapter override, Work/Step-only Submission writers, Evidence-only Claim writers, same-Store crash cuts, one-winner submit/renew/takeover/amend/revoke/cancel races and same-key replay; add, remove, replace, node-change, edge-change, Gate-change, authority-change, effect-change, split, and merge matrices; exact retain-state by zero/one/invalid/duplicate/conflicting satisfaction-carry matrices across every old lifecycle state and every other carry class; old-satisfaction/amendment, Lease, Submission, cancellation, continuation and concurrent-amendment races; Lease acquire, renew, expiry, continuation, stale submission, satisfaction, amendment, and highest-fence races; self-removing amendment and fault injection at every write boundary; purpose-specific equivalence and deliberate laundering attacks; completion and acceptance interleavings; in-doubt connector effects and compensation; large-DAG and Claim-set transaction bounds; adapter and Packet parity; sealed export and restore equality; and fixtures for every v1 Task, Progress, blocker, gate, dependency, one- and many-Claim submission, compound assertion, assignment, and verification form.

Reopen this decision only if a legitimate runtime mutation cannot bind one generation-scoped Step subject; correct execution requires two Contract Generations to accept current mutations simultaneously; a safe amendment requires partial graph activation; purpose-specific equivalence cannot preserve useful work without granting old-root tokens current authority; stable Step identity cannot coexist with immutable terminal binding history; or a legitimate Run cannot have exactly one owner in the closed ExecutionAttempt union.

Reopen the effective a13b Submission/Claim boundary only if a legitimate Work or Step Submission can contain zero Claims; one Claim must legitimately bind multiple Submissions; Claims must legitimately be appended after Submission commit; Work/Step-owned Submission and Evidence-owned Claim sole writers cannot publish through one atomic same-Store carrier; deterministic finite Claim-set identity cannot be defined; lossless migration requires proposition split/merge inference or data loss; or a supported adapter cannot preserve the same owner and cardinality semantics without private authority. Foreign keys, aggregate navigation, module placement and implementation convenience are not reopen grounds.

The locked execution lifecycle sharpens continuation: amendment closes the old 1:1 StepLease-StepAttempt pair and every term under it. Purpose-specific execution equivalence plus fresh authority may create only a linked new-root pair with a higher Step fence, initial LeaseTerm, remaining cumulative budget, and zero transferred Runs. An old Run is never reparented. A fresh Session cannot convert old-root physical activity into current execution, and a Takeover Safety Proof is required before overlapping new-root work can touch the same shared or effect boundary.

#### Remote effects and reconciliation

Effect Intent is the stable durable semantic identity for one potentially side-effecting remote or protected operation. It is not owned by the lifetime of a Step Lease, StepAttempt, DispatchAttempt, ReconciliationAttempt, Run, process, Session, Message, current Step membership, Contract Generation, Store Generation or Authority Epoch. Every Intent belongs to exactly one immutable `EffectIntentHomeV1`, carries exactly one immutable typed Effect Origin and freezes exactly one `EffectIntentOriginationFenceV1`. Execution owns the Intent, fences, DispatchAttempt and ReconciliationAttempt records, and local Remote Classification. Evidence owns remote Observations and Assessments. Local classification is never actual provider truth by itself.

`EffectIntentHomeV1` is the closed union `ActiveStoreHomeV1 | NoStoreCeremonyHomeV1 | PreStoreCeremonyHomeV1`. Active Store binds exactly one stable RepositoryDomain or InstallationDomain identity, realm and semantic namespace; its origin fence binds the exact originating Store, Generation, Epoch, material token, Action Request, authority basis, Receipt, Result and dispatch reservation. No Store is legal only for `InstallationContextGenesis`; its home binds the protected realm and Locator-candidate branch but fabricates no active DomainId, Generation or Epoch, while its origin fence binds the exact CeremonySpec, sealed commitment, AttemptId, candidate bundle/seal, carrier incarnation, expected-old token and external anchor. Pre Store binds one exact inactive Repository or Installation Ceremony branch and destination lineage; its origin fence binds the exact Ceremony, branch bundle/seal, carrier, expected-old token, AttemptId and external basis.

Every later DispatchAttempt or Action-origin ReconciliationAttempt binds one fresh same-home `EffectIntentUseFenceV1`. Active-store use binds the current same-domain Generation, Epoch, namespace and material token plus fresh authority, credentials, Attempt fence and provider guards. A new Generation or Epoch kills the old use fence but does not reparent or duplicate the Intent. No-store and pre-store Ceremony origins structurally reject ReconciliationAttempt. Their exact same-Attempt `ResolveResult` creates no Intent, DispatchAttempt, ReconciliationAttempt, provider key, redispatch or Run and may perform only one bounded proven-effect-free exact-attempt lookup under fresh branch authority.

The home branch is derived from frozen EffectOriginRoute context and the exact Operation subject before authorization. Action routes are Active Store; `InstallationContextGenesis` is No Store; every other Ceremony route is Pre Store. Caller, adapter, Skill, Recipe, provider, path, carrier metadata and migration input never select or translate the home. At most one live Intent exists for one home-qualified semantic-operation key. Another domain may retain only a non-bearer reference. A genuinely shared provider effect has one authoritative home or is unavailable; Maestro claims no global cross-domain lock, classification, deduplication or transaction.

Every Intent also records the one originating `ActionRequestV1 | CeremonyRequestV1`, matching Authorization Receipt and Result as immutable non-bearer provenance. For the Action branch, the 2a07 law incorporated by the current composite head requires the exact leaf to select exactly one ActionAuthorityBasisV1: ordinary leaves retain current Session plus live Grant/Mandate authority, while exact CMA leaves use only their current branch, phase slot, executor assertion and applicability. The Ceremony branch uses only its exact externally anchored no-store or pre-store basis and never donates an Action basis. Neither the Effect Origin, originating records, Message, prior Intent, Session nor old Step authority authorizes dispatch, reconciliation, remediation, applicability or another operation. Every ReconciliationAttempt binds a fresh Action Request and independently evaluates its leaf's one current basis; Ceremony `ResolveResult` is no-Run and uses no ReconciliationAttempt.

##### Effect origin algebra and staged closure

The design owns a Candidate Effect Origin Manifest until every effecting context closes. Candidate rows have no runtime consumer and cannot be advertised, accepted, dispatched, reconciled, or extended by adapters, connectors, Recipes, profiles, providers, callbacks, metadata, or plugins. A later total-coverage Decision freezes a closed exhaustive EffectOriginV1 before ActionSpecV1 freezes. Every variant declares one canonical source owner, closed immutable subject schema, exact semantic uniqueness key, allowed originating Action leaves, authority and credential basis, forbidden fields, retention and security-erasure behavior, migration mapping, adapter parity, and crash, replay, race, and noninterference proof. Unknown variants and fields fail closed. There is no generic Action Request, connector, provider, callback, metadata, or plugin origin.

The minimum final union already contains three forced variants:

- **Step Effect Origin** binds one exact generation-scoped Step Binding, StepAttempt, StepLease fence, and current LeaseTerm ordinal and hash at the Intent-origination commit. Only this variant may carry Work, Contract Root, Step, Lease, or LeaseTerm origin fields. Once the Intent commits, all Step references are immutable provenance only. Amendment, removal, supersession, terminal Work, Lease expiry, and pair closure never delete, reparent, neutralize, or authorize it.
- **Coordination Delivery Origin** is an inline closed origin value binding one immutable Message reference and semantic hash, exact logical recipient, exact Coordination-owned Delivery Subject, and delivery-purpose hash. One Message may source zero or more Intents, one per exact recipient-subject-purpose tuple, and at most one live Intent represents the same semantic tuple. A changed recipient, subject, or purpose is a new explicitly authorized operation. This variant carries no Work, Contract Root, Step, Lease, lifecycle, dependency, authority, read-state, or Remote Classification field. The Coordination Decision rejects a duplicate one-to-one Coordination Delivery Intent and fixes local Message publication and remote delivery origination as separate actions: the Message commits first; Originate Coordination Delivery later commits this Intent and its dispatch reservation; a crash between them is local-only and no adapter may infer delivery, send remotely first, or append a fallback after ambiguity.
- **Effect Remediation Origin** binds one exact prior Effect Intent, one closed relation of cancels or compensates, and one remediation semantic-subject hash. It carries no Step Lease and inherits no authority, credential, provider key, budget, classification, applicability, or blocker scope. Its graph is self-edge-free, creation-ordered, acyclic, and semantically unique. The new Intent uses fresh authority, credentials, key, fence, budget, uncertainty, and reconciliation and never rewrites the original.

Current evidence forces no fourth variant. Governed release, deploy, and publish may remain Step-origin; external GitHub workflows remain external orchestration. Local install, sync, update, erasure, garbage collection, and Store activation remain separately staged filesystem or Distribution protocols. Effect-free remote acquisition creates no Intent unless its pinned Provider Operation Contract establishes a side effect. A future first-class repository release, managed model call, research connector, remote erasure, or other non-Step effect must receive a separate owner-specific variant through its context Decision or be proven Step-origin, external-pattern, or effect-free before closure.

Before any network I/O, a short SQLite transaction commits the Effect Intent, exact Effect Origin, semantic-operation and uniqueness hashes, originating request/receipt/result references, provider, account or tenant, audience or region, operation, target, canonical request payload hash, Connector Credential Binding revision, Provider Operation Contract hash, provider idempotency policy and key, replay-safe horizon, reconciliation policy and visibility window, response interpreter, remediation policy, authority and budget consumption, local Action Result, and idempotency record. Credentials never enter Maestro. One semantic operation has at most one live Intent across origin variants, and the same provider key with any different origin subject, payload, account, operation, target, audience, region, or provider contract rejects.

A Provider Operation Contract is immutable and locally pinned. It defines request canonicalization, the precise boundary at which bytes may cause an effect, provider key scope and retention, parameter-mismatch behavior, asynchronous acknowledgement semantics, authoritative query or correlation method, eventual-consistency window, response and callback verification, postcondition classifier, and whether cancellation or compensation exists. Unknown, unavailable, expired, or changed capability fails closed rather than consulting ambient SDK behavior or current online documentation.

The closed Remote Classifications are:

```text
prepared
  -> dispatching
  -> pending
   | in_doubt
   | confirmed_applied
   | confirmed_not_applied
   | partially_applied
   | conflicted

pending | in_doubt | partially_applied | conflicted
  -> reconciled classification

confirmed_not_applied -> dispatching
  only when same-intent redispatch is currently authorized and proven safe

prepared | confirmed_not_applied -> cancelled
```

Prepared means durable intent exists before I/O. Dispatching means one durable Dispatch Attempt and dispatch fence exist. Pending means the provider acknowledged asynchronous work while the declared postcondition remains unobserved. In_doubt is mandatory when the request may have crossed the effect boundary without conclusive remote Observation. Partially_applied and conflicted require explicit reconciliation, compensation, or human resolution. Cancelled is valid only before dispatch or after confirmed non-application. Confirmed_applied and cancelled are terminal for the original Intent.

The nine classification values are visible only through one home-local atomic control product. `EffectIntentControlHeadV1` is the sole mutable selector and points to one immutable `EffectIntentControlRevisionV1` plus one `EffectIntentControlWriterTermV1`. The revision joins the DispatchAttempt-history root, zero or one current live Attempt revision, one immutable classification revision, live dispatch, dispatch-fence high-water and carrier occurrence reference, authority/effect-slot/dispatch-budget accounting, current material/credential/use-fence commitments, Run-set closure, local Result/idempotency publication and control health. No component row is independently current. Physical normalization is permitted only behind the one expected-old Head CAS.

The live-state compatibility relation is exact: `EffectIntentLiveDispatchV1 = None | Reserved | Sealed`; exactly ten of the 27 live-dispatch/classification pairs are valid. `None` combines with `prepared | pending | in_doubt | confirmed_applied | confirmed_not_applied | partially_applied | conflicted | cancelled`; `Reserved` combines only with `dispatching`; `Sealed` combines only with `in_doubt`. All other seventeen combinations fail closed as integrity-blocked or quarantined before I/O or Projection. Integrity block is outside the nine-value classification grammar. Compatibility is not reachability: origin, authority, prior-state, Attempt-outcome and currentness guards narrow it further.

`EffectIntentControlTransitionV1` binds the exact Intent/Home, expected Head/revision/writer term, candidate immutable revision and Head, current typed Action or Ceremony request, outgoing and incoming authority terms, debit and idempotency, and exactly one carrier. `ActiveStoreAtomic` publishes all component revisions and the Head swap in one serializable same-Store transaction. `NoStoreProtectedCas` and `PreStoreProtectedCas` publish the complete sealed revision closure through the exact branch carrier and expected-old token; uncertain CAS occurrence uses exact-Attempt readback. CAS losers, stale requests and same-key replay publish no revision, spend nothing and perform no protected or network I/O.

One Effect Intent owns 0..N immutable DispatchAttempts, 0..N immutable ReconciliationAttempts, zero or one Head-selected live dispatch and exactly one current Control Head. Evidence owns the 0..N remote Observations and reconciliation Assessments that bind the Intent as subject or provenance. Each dispatch Run is owned by exactly one DispatchAttempt that binds this Intent and its dispatch fence. Pre-reservation validation failure creates no DispatchAttempt. The exact closed algebra is `DispatchAttemptStateV1 = ReservedUnsealedV1 | SealedInFlightV1 | TerminalV1(DispatchAttemptTerminalV1)`, where `DispatchAttemptTerminalV1 = PreSealLocallyRejectedV1 | SealedDispatchTerminalV1`. A reserved Attempt begins as `ReservedUnsealedV1`, with no terminal value and a structurally absent `DispatchCrossingSealV1`. Terminal Attempt revisions remain reachable immutable history but never become a current selector.

`ReservedUnsealedV1` has zero seals and zero terminal outcomes. `SealedInFlightV1` has exactly one immutable `DispatchCrossingSealV1` and zero terminal outcomes. `TerminalV1(PreSealLocallyRejectedV1)` structurally owns no seal, fixes the outcome to `locally_rejected`, binds exact post-reservation local refusal evidence and proves by CAS that no seal won. `TerminalV1(SealedDispatchTerminalV1)` carries exactly the same seal from `SealedInFlightV1` and fixes the outcome to exactly `definitely_not_sent | response_received | ambiguous_transport`. The exhaustive `DispatchAttemptOutcomeV1` projection therefore remains exactly four members. Unknown tags, sealed local rejection, unsealed remote outcome, outcome on a nonterminal state, seal replacement, direct reserved-to-sealed-terminal transition and every terminal escape reject.

Before any application envelope release, one durable Control-Head CAS appends the exact `SealedInFlightV1` revision, commits the sole seal and atomically changes `Reserved/dispatching` to `Sealed/in_doubt`, binding the Attempt revision, current same-home use fence, immutable envelope commitment, Provider Operation Contract, provider scope/key, credential commitment, authority basis, dispatch fence, material stamp, Run-set revision and accounting closure. The successful seal-CAS caller alone receives one ephemeral non-serializable capability to perform the one release in that live adapter invocation. Reading, replaying, restoring or recovering persisted state never reconstructs that capability and performs zero new I/O. Reservation alone never permits release. No transport or response Run starts without the seal; preparation Runs remain owned by the same DispatchAttempt. No network call occurs inside a database transaction. A pre-seal local-rejection transition and the seal transition race on the same Control Head: exactly one wins, and the loser writes, consumes and crosses nothing.

`SealedInFlightV1` may remain durably visible indefinitely when no authorized driver or conclusive Evidence can classify it. `definitely_not_sent` requires conclusive durable connector proof that no bytes crossed the declared boundary. An exact completed response under the pinned response predicate yields `response_received`, which proves transport completion but not remote application. Partial bytes leave the Attempt `SealedInFlightV1`; EOF, timeout, cancellation, partial stream, lost control or crash after possible crossing without exact completion yields `ambiguous_transport` and Intent `in_doubt`. Adapter unavailability discovered after the seal, including a sealed crash before actual release, is `definitely_not_sent` only with conclusive no-crossing proof and otherwise `ambiguous_transport`; it can never become `locally_rejected`. Redirects, authentication challenges and provider errors are responses to the original Attempt; following them is a fresh higher-dispatch-fence Attempt. Hidden SDK/transport retry or redirect makes the adapter unavailable.

The only legal transitions are `ReservedUnsealedV1 -> TerminalV1(PreSealLocallyRejectedV1)` and `ReservedUnsealedV1 -> SealedInFlightV1 -> TerminalV1(SealedDispatchTerminalV1)`. The terminal CAS commits exactly one terminal tag plus inherited common bindings. The pre-seal branch binds exact local-refusal evidence and no seal; the sealed branch carries the identical immutable seal and applicable response, no-crossing or ambiguity basis. Same-key replay returns the exact visible state or committed Result, performs zero I/O and never resumes implicitly.

At the Control-Head level, pre-seal local rejection changes `Reserved/dispatching` to `None/confirmed_not_applied`. A sealed `definitely_not_sent` terminal changes `Sealed/in_doubt` to `None/confirmed_not_applied`; `ambiguous_transport` changes it to `None/in_doubt`; `response_received` changes it only through the pinned evaluator to `None/pending | in_doubt | confirmed_applied | confirmed_not_applied | partially_applied | conflicted`. Terminal Attempt append, complete Run closure, live-dispatch clearing, classification/accounting and Result/idempotency are one atomic write set. At the d21e predecessor checkpoint, `None/cancelled` was structurally valid but intentionally unreachable. Effective efa0 incorporates 3905 and makes it reachable only through the exact no-I/O ordinary, Bootstrap-G0 or CMA Action withdrawal branch or the matching `Withdraw` Ceremony mode, under the one-Head CAS and proof law in the effective section above; no adapter, legacy label or adjacent lifecycle may infer it.

Typed recovery is `DispatchReservationModeV1::RecoverReserved` on one of the four existing reserve Action leaves or `CeremonyRequestModeV1::RecoverReserved` on the same exact Ceremony. It targets the same durable Intent and same `ReservedUnsealedV1` DispatchAttempt under a distinct recovery idempotency binding and fresh current same-home authorization. It binds the original route/spec, Home, Attempt revision, origination/use/dispatch fences, envelope commitment, provider scope/key/contract, credential commitment, material stamp, effect slot and budgets. It creates or remints none of them and cannot refresh stale basis inside the Attempt. A successful recovery may commit exact pre-seal local rejection or the sole seal; only the live seal-CAS winner may release the exact envelope once. Same-key replay, every CAS loser, `SealedInFlightV1`, terminal state, restore and later recovery perform zero release I/O and consume no new effect or dispatch budget. Later send under changed basis requires a fresh separately authorized higher-fence Attempt.

The original handler, recovery callers, rejection, seal, response handler, terminalizer, classifier, reconciler and same-home restore writer CAS the same Control Head and exact joined revision; one writer wins and every loser writes, consumes and crosses nothing. Missing or contradictory recovery basis, independently advanced components, or possible crossing without a seal is an integrity fault outside the legal algebra: it fabricates no in-flight state, seal, outcome, success, Run or retry right and blocks matching origination and redispatch. Recovery of `SealedInFlightV1` never releases again and may only classify conclusive no-crossing, exact completion or ambiguity. Terminalization atomically appends terminal Attempt history, closes or disposes all Runs, clears live dispatch, publishes the pinned classification/accounting and local Result/idempotency, permanently refuses later Run reservation, and allows no terminal escape. A late authenticated response is only an immutable Observation for a home-legal fresh classification path; it never reopens, rewrites, resends or implies success.

Remote responses, callbacks, polling results, signed receipts, retained provider snapshots, and manual adjudication are typed Observations under the Evidence model. A separately authorized ReconciliationAttempt binds this Intent plus one fresh authorized Action Request and owns every reconciliation Run in that try. It verifies exact provider identity, account, target, operation, request hash, correlation, authenticity, time and visibility basis, then a pinned evaluator derives the classification. With live dispatch `None`, one Control-Head transition atomically appends the Attempt/Run closure and new immutable classification revision; reconciliation never creates another selector. All applicable Observations remain immutable. Equally applicable disagreement, several matching remote objects, wrong-account results, forged callbacks, parameter mismatch, unavailable truth, or incomplete postconditions remain conflicted or in_doubt; newest never wins.

Maestro local Action Request idempotency deduplicates canonical local publication. Provider idempotency belongs to the Effect Intent. A generic-profile safe redispatch uses the same Intent, semantic hash, provider scope and provider key and creates a fresh higher-fence Attempt. It is advertised only from Head state `None/confirmed_not_applied`, while attempt and time budgets remain, live authority and credential binding cover the exact action, and either the pinned provider guarantee still protects the exact key and semantic request or the prior attempt is proved definitely_not_sent. The 5f23 External High-water profile cross-rejects same-Intent redispatch: after DefinitelyDidNotOccur, another try requires a separately authorized new Intent, AttemptId, provider key, prospective record commitment and debit. A fresh key is never automatic after uncertainty or expiry.

If provider idempotency is absent, unknown, expired, differently scoped, or contradicted, any possible dispatch permits only authoritative readback, exact human adjudication, or separately authorized compensation. Eventual-consistency not-found remains in_doubt until the pinned visibility window passes. A provider that retains failures under a key, rejects parameter mismatch, or cannot authoritatively query the operation is handled according to its pinned contract rather than generic retry assumptions.

Local timeout, cancellation request, process exit, Lease expiry, HTTP acceptance, Contract amendment, Step cancellation, Message read state, or origin removal never proves remote success, failure, or cancellation. For Step Effect Origin, a stale worker may submit attributable historical Observation material through a fresh authenticated action but cannot dispatch, redispatch, reconcile current state, submit, satisfy, or complete under the old token. Same-domain restore or recovery preserves Intent home, origin, origination fence, Attempt history and the exact legal Control product while Epoch/Generation change kills every old Session, Lease, connector authority, dispatch authority and use fence. After exact same-home continuity and old-writer fencing, one `SameHomeRestore` writer term may become current; a fresh `ReconcileEffectIntent` may then refine classification without minting an Intent or redispatching. Clone/import into another DomainId preserves source-qualified non-bearer history only; it cannot acquire a writer term, create a second Head or matching Intent, and unresolved history blocks unsafe activation until explicit migration resolution.

A pending, in_doubt, partially_applied, conflicted, or unresolved applied effect survives origin replacement and removal and blocks duplicate semantic Intent creation, blind retry, unsafe origin disposition, and migration activation until the pinned policy accepts confirmed reconciliation, proven-unaffected disposition, remediation, or human resolution. It blocks Step Submission or Work completion only when its Step Effect Origin is current-material or an independently published Contract or Gate makes the remote effect material. Coordination delivery and remediation lineage cannot acquire Step blocker scope by reference. Removal is never remote cancellation.

Remote cancellation and compensation are new separately authorized Effect Intents whose Effect Remediation Origin links the exact original Intent with cancels or compensates and an exact remediation subject hash. Each has its own semantic hash, Provider Operation Contract, credential binding, provider key, dispatch fence and Attempts, budget, uncertainty, reconciliation, and failure modes. The original history never changes. Projection may describe the pair as compensated only after the compensation Intent is confirmed applied; that statement does not prove restoration of every external condition.

External schedulers remain external. They may poll current Agent Packets and invoke advertised dispatch or reconciliation Action Specs through their own Principal, Session, Grant, limits, and connector bridge. They cannot read SQLite directly, hold Maestro secrets, invent retry safety, own lifecycle, or make Maestro run continuously. Without an external driver, a stranded Intent remains visibly pending or in doubt.

Migration preserves every legacy source byte before interpretation: channel messages, cursors and delivery receipts; hook and session JSONL; derived Run summaries; command logs; provider URLs and identifiers; release, deploy, publish and deletion artifacts; actor and claim text; verification and proof records; timestamps, ordering, paths, and store provenance. Current Codex-thread delivery sends remote turn/start before recording, may create no local Message on success, and may append a local fallback after an ambiguous error; its open-string delivered receipt has no Message identity and proves neither uniqueness nor completed delivery. Current work-lease ids, claimed_by, in_progress, Message or Receipt text, Session, hook status, URL, command exit, autonomy row, and verification report mint no Effect Origin, Effect Intent, DispatchAttempt, provider classification, authority, or retry safety. The current execution lifecycle is carried by effective head efa0 through its complete incorporation of a13b, 3905, d21e, d116, 7138 and af45, which in turn incorporates ebcd, 31b3, 92f7, 6875, 2a07 and b17f ancestry. ##### Step execution tenure

One StepLease and one StepAttempt are created and closed atomically in strict 1:1 cardinality for one exact Step Binding, one monotonically increasing Step fence, one executor Principal, and one continuous authority tenure. Acquisition fixes the Contract Root, Store Generation, Authority Epoch, authority and effect envelope, resources, deadlines, attempt and Run limits, and cumulative budgets. It consumes current execution authority, records the Receipt, Action Result, and idempotency result, and moves Work ready to active when this is the first execution. Neither record exists, reopens, or terminates without the other.

The live pair closes exactly once as submitted, yielded, failed, cancelled, timed_out, lost, or fenced. Submitted atomically creates the Step-owned Submission and its complete finite non-empty canonical set of Evidence-owned Claims, records the `SubmissionClaimSetV1` digest and moves Step open to submitted. Every other pair result leaves Step open unless the same amendment transaction cancels or supersedes it. Submission rejection may return the Step to open, but execution repair always uses a linked new pair and a new immutable Claim set. Expiry is effective at trusted as_of greater than or equal to expires_at; no hidden worker writes time transitions.

##### Renewal and Session continuity

Each Lease has one CAS current-term head. LeaseTerms are immutable, contiguous, and hash-linked and bind Lease, Attempt, fence, ordinal, prior term, issue time, expiry, and hard deadline. Renewal is a fresh authorized Action Request before expiry and only for the same binding, root, Store Generation, Authority Epoch, executor Principal, and fixed envelope. It appends one term and cannot widen authority or resources, extend the hard deadline, reset attempts, Runs, duration, Grant capacity, or budgets, or borrow a later term's expiry. Same-key replay returns the original term.

Every Run or segment reservation, current Step execution action, Step Effect Origin origination, current-applicable Step outcome, pair close, Submission, satisfaction request, renewal, or Step mutation binds the exact current term ordinal and hash as well as root, binding, fence, revisions, time, and live authority. A Coordination Delivery Origin or Effect Remediation Origin binds no LeaseTerm and inherits no Step authority. Hash linkage is audit integrity; the Store term head, fence, exact-root checks, and transaction CAS provide fencing. Heartbeat is only an Observation and Projection hint.

StepAttempt fixes one verified executor Principal, not one Session. A newly authenticated Session for that same Principal may continue the unexpired pair only through a fresh term-bound Action Request and current Grant, revocation, assurance, and budget evaluation. A different Principal, executor handoff, expiry, lost exclusive control, repair, recovery, takeover, yield/resume, cancellation recovery, or root continuation requires a fresh higher-fence pair. Session, Lease, Attempt, heartbeat, and prior Receipt are never bearer authority.

##### Runs and retry

A StepAttempt owns a finite bounded Run set. Each Run is reserved durably before execution and binds one immutable semantic-operation hash, inputs, environment, target, declared execution boundary, deadline, owner, and current term where Step-owned. Its closed graph is reserved to active or definitely_not_started, cancelled, timed_out, lost, or fenced; active to succeeded, failed, cancelled, timed_out, lost, or fenced. A terminal Run never reopens or reparents, and finite recording does not prove the process stopped.

A Run segment or reconnect is a bounded append-only linear continuation of the same proven process or provider-job identity. It invokes nothing new and cannot reset owner, term, deadline, budget, or control. If identity or exclusive control cannot be proven, the Run becomes lost. Runs never form a normative DAG.

A same-Attempt launch retry is a new Run permitted only after the predecessor conclusively records definitely_not_started or a pinned equivalent proving its execution boundary was not crossed. It keeps the semantic-operation hash, increments the launch ordinal, and consumes budget. If the operation may have started, repeating it after any terminal result is a new causal try and therefore a new higher-fence pair. Distinct planned operations and pinned sampling repetitions use distinct operation identities.

##### Takeover and Submission

Lease expiry, heartbeat loss, cancellation request, timeout, and process absence fence Maestro mutations but never prove physical quiescence. Takeover blocks unless pinned Evidence proves complete quiescence, an enforced revocable sandbox excludes every later shared or effect publication, or attempt-isolated resources are mechanically fenced at every shared, promotion, and connector boundary. Worktree naming or process absence alone is insufficient. Unknown overlap yields a blocked reconciliation or human-resolution path.

Submission is one current-pair same-Store serializable transaction. It requires the live unexpired term, exact Run-set revision, no active or physically uncertain relevant Run, current Work, root, binding, Gate Snapshot, Store Generation, Authority Epoch, revocation and authority state, one valid finite non-empty canonical Claim set with closed Observation references, current applicability, and no unresolved material Effect Intent. It creates one Step-owned Submission and the complete Evidence-owned Claim set under their separate sole writers, stores the `SubmissionClaimSetV1` digest, moves Step open to submitted, and closes the pair as submitted. Expected-old races have one winner; same-key same-digest replay returns the original records; every stale or changed-meaning loser creates no orphan Claim or Submission. Satisfaction remains a separate Gate and authority action.

One DispatchAttempt may own bounded preparation, transport, and response Runs but permits at most one possible application-level crossing of the pinned Provider Operation Contract effect boundary. `crossing_possible` seals the one-crossing budget before release; it is terminal for sending, not for the whole Attempt. ##### Locked algebra law

- At a frozen version, ActionSpec is a closed exhaustive two-level sum. A top-level family routes to exactly one primary owner; a leaf names one semantic action with a closed canonical payload and statically declared cross-context participants.
- One Action Request selects one leaf. There is no generic CRUD, transition, apply, invoke, import, arbitrary or heterogeneous batch, nested action list, callback program, argv or shell action, Recipe program, adapter action, plugin registry, open kind string, or behavior-bearing metadata map.
- Every frozen leaf binds typed subjects; exact Store Generation, Authority Epoch, Contract Root and record heads; expected revisions and hashes; live authority requirement; typed prerequisite Receipt slots; effect, idempotency, retry and auto-safe classes; fixed atomic publication set; produced records; forbidden effects; migration mapping; adapter parity; and race, crash, replay and reopen proof.
- Unknown family, leaf, field, payload, semantic kind, or required protocol capability fails closed. A new leaf requires negotiated core-version evolution, migration and parity rules, and proof.
- Reads, inspection, Projection, pure evaluation, Recipe sequencing and external orchestration are not actions. A read that persists an acknowledgement or other fact splits that mutation into its own leaf.
- Action Result is local phase truth only. Evidence, Gate truth, remote success, physical deletion, consumer restart, and Store activation require their own exact records or later phases.

##### Authority and idempotency

A runtime Action leaf statically selects exactly one request basis. An ordinary request is authenticated by verified Principal and current Session proof and authorized by live unrevoked Grant paths plus required available Mandates. A pre-store request uses only its exact closed ceremony proof. A CMA request uses only its exact non-Session CMA branch, purpose slot, fresh executor assertion and applicability. Earlier Authorization Receipts may fill only leaf-specific non-bearer prerequisite slots. Actor text, Session identity alone, Packet, Lease, Attempt, prior Result, Receipt, origin or candidate never grants permission, and no basis may fall back to another.

Same idempotency key plus the same canonical semantic request returns the original Result. The same key plus different meaning is a hard conflict. A new key cannot bypass stale expected material, revocation, exhausted budget, consumed Mandate, fence, or protocol phase. A rejected or losing stale request consumes no authority or mutation budget.

Compound leaves contain no child action list, child idempotency keys, or child Results.
