### Full-seal scheduling for the active build

Full proof coverage remains mandatory, but full multi-engine reexecution is scheduled at the deepest useful seam instead of being amplified through every predecessor and intermediate Stage. A previously committed and certified Stage is an immutable predecessor: downstream work verifies its exact commit, tree, artifact identities, receipts and complete declared dependency closure through read-only equality checks and content-addressed reconstruction. It does not rerun that predecessor's full behavior/mutant seal merely because a later Stage, design-provenance record or execution-only scheduling amendment changed. A mismatched predecessor byte cannot be blessed by a cached receipt: the downstream Stage must either restore the exact certified predecessor or bind the changed byte in its own current dependency closure and leave the predecessor's historical receipt immutable.

The active main implementation runs one full multi-engine seal for Stage 5 only. That Stage-5 seal binds the exact admitted Stage-0-through-4 predecessor identities plus every current Stage-5 source, test, validator, generated artifact and proof byte; it does not recursively rerun the complete Stage-0-through-4 full seals. Cheap identity, ancestry, hermeticity and focused falsifiers still fail closed before Stage 5 freezes.

Stages 6 through 12 do not run a separate full multi-engine seal after each integration. Each Stage must still pass its complete focused compile/tests, formatting, strict lint, hermeticity, cheap mutant/proof preflight, fresh correctness/authority-race/proof review, real-upstream parity and broad cross-Stage integration gate before its scoped integration commit. Those commits are `integrated_unsealed`: durable recovery checkpoints only, not certification, currentness, release readiness or permission to weaken a later proof.

After Stage 12 is completely integrated, the orchestrator freezes the entire Stage-0-through-12 source, test, validator, artifact and proof closure and runs exactly one cumulative full-chain independent multi-engine seal. That final seal reexecutes every required behavior, mutation, crash/race, authority, migration, adapter-parity, removal and ancestry proof against the final tree. Only its successful receipt-bound readback may promote the integrated Stage 6-through-12 chain from `integrated_unsealed` to `certified`. A failure identifies the smallest owning Stage, invalidates its checkpoint and every dependent checkpoint, and requires a corrected sequential reintegration before one new final frozen candidate may seal. No partial final seal, cached shared verdict or prior intermediate gate substitutes for that reexecution.

This scheduling changes execution cost and recovery granularity only. It changes no Contract, Stage deliverable, proof case, acceptance criterion, authority transition, migration rule, removal gate or public behavior. Reopen Design if the final full-chain runner cannot independently reproduce a proof formerly supplied only by an intermediate Stage seal.

### Parallel candidate-execution overlay for Stages 6 through 12

The Stage table above remains the sole canonical integration order and final-certification dependency order. Starting with Stage 6, its prerequisite column is not a prohibition on isolated downstream candidate implementation after the Stage-5 boundary is stable. An external Codex orchestrator may keep at most six Stage candidate threads active while canonical merge and proof publication remain sequential and the only full-chain seal remains after Stage 12. This overlay changes implementation order only. It creates no Maestro scheduler, queue, lifecycle, authority, Action, Receipt, Stage state or product-scope exception, and it changes no Stage deliverable, proof case, Contract identity or public behavior.

Parallel execution may begin only after Stage 5 has one stable committed and certified boundary and the orchestrator has created one exact fanout base commit. That commit closes the frozen Stage-0 contracts and Stage-1-through-5 interfaces consumed downstream, predeclares any shared module facades needed for disjoint work, and records an exact nonoverlapping path-ownership manifest plus shared-file denylist. A dirty Stage-5 worktree, changing proof source, unresolved receipt, uncommitted interface or mismatched Contract identity blocks fanout.

The external execution vocabulary is deliberately noncanonical:

- `candidate`: isolated implementation in one dedicated worktree at the exact fanout base, tested only through frozen interfaces, canonical vectors and real internal seams or test adapters;
- `candidate_ready`: the worker's complete owned slice has focused compile, test, lint, hermeticity and cheap proof preflight plus fresh correctness, authority/race and proof-coverage review, but has not entered the canonical branch;
- `integration_ready`: the candidate has been rebased onto the certified immediate predecessor, every test adapter has either been replaced by the real upstream implementation or proven to remain an internal test-only seam, and cross-Stage contract/parity proof passes;
- `integrated_unsealed`: the orchestrator alone has integrated the Stage on its exact predecessor, passed every non-full Stage gate and committed a scoped recovery checkpoint, but the Stage remains noncurrent and uncertified until the post-Stage-12 full-chain seal;
- `certified`: Stage 5 after its current-Stage seal, or the complete Stage 6-through-12 chain only after the final cumulative full-chain seal and receipt-bound readback.

These labels are external workbench descriptions only. They are not persisted or interpreted by Maestro and cannot be translated into Work, Step, Run, Result, Evidence, approval, currentness or completion. `candidate_ready` never satisfies a Stage prerequisite. A downstream candidate may finish early and wait; after Stage 5, it cannot merge before every predecessor named in the canonical table has its required `integrated_unsealed` checkpoint, and no Stage 6-through-12 checkpoint may activate behavior or claim certification before the final full-chain seal.

#### Maximum-six candidate wave

The initial fanout after Stage 5 is exactly Stage candidates 6 through 11. Stage 12 is queued until one of those six threads releases a slot. Stage 12 may then prepare read-only consumer censuses, architecture guards, negative compatibility fixtures and release-proof inputs, but its production removal, source-namespace promotion and pruning remain unavailable until Stage 11 is certified.

| Candidate thread | Parallel-owned implementation | Frozen dependency used during candidate work | Mandatory sequential integration boundary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Stage 6 | Projection, Packet/Operation/Result transport, Action submission and replay, CLI/JSON and generated capability catalog | certified Stages 1 through 5 plus Stage-0 public contracts | integrates first after Stage 5; no downstream candidate is merged before the Stage 6 `integrated_unsealed` checkpoint |
| Stage 7 | Orchestration and Recipe application/return, Planning and Scheduling Assessment, Coordination and Inbox | Stage-0 Recipe/Job/Packet schemas plus canonical ActionFrontier, ActionRef, WaveRef and Packet fixtures | rebase onto integrated Stage 6; replace or parity-prove every Projection/transport test adapter before integration |
| Stage 8 | Search, Memory, Intake, Research, Capability/Maturity and Observation-facing diagnostics | certified owner interfaces from Stages 1 through 5 plus frozen Stage-6/7 value contracts and vectors | rebase onto integrated Stage 7; prove coherent-snapshot and non-authority parity against real Projection, Planning and Orchestration |
| Stage 9 | Distribution and Installation transaction core, target identity/custody, snapshot catalog, recovery, currentness and domain-local publication | Stage-0 Resource/Bundle/Release and cutover contracts plus certified Persistence, Authority, Execution and effect seams | rebase onto integrated Stage 8; Stage 9 retains mutation/currentness ownership while Stage 8 consumes its facts only |
| Stage 10 | two read-only MCP adapters and host descriptors; one Skill/bootstrap tree; TUI, hooks, shell, schemas, external patterns and connectors | exact public/resource fixtures and the frozen interfaces of Stages 6 through 9 | rebase onto integrated Stage 9; real Packet/catalog/Recipe/Installation wiring, host skew and complete adapter parity must pass |
| Stage 11 | byte-total inventory, deterministic classification and identity map, quarantine, inactive-store import, migration fixtures and consumer closure | Stage-0 migration/cutover contracts, frozen v1 census and test adapters for Stage-9/10 effects and public consumers | rebase onto integrated Stage 10; real domain cutover, association finality, old-client refusal and consumer-zero proof remain sequential |
| Stage 12 | initially no production mutation; later consumer-zero audit, namespace-move preparation, negative compatibility and release-proof preparation | integrated source and retained-reader manifests as they become available | production deletion, canonical namespace promotion, pruning and release-proof preparation begin only after the Stage 11 `integrated_unsealed` checkpoint; certification waits for the final full-chain seal |

This split follows semantic ownership rather than convenient file grouping. Stage 6 owns CLI/JSON transport; Stage 10 may consume but not redefine it. Stage 9 owns Installation mutation, claims, currentness and snapshots; Stage 10 owns adapter/resource rendering and host integration only. Stage 9 and the exact domain owners retain cutover effects and currentness; Stage 11 owns source classification, association meaning, quarantine and inactive import only. Stage 8 Capability/Maturity consumes Distribution and Installation facts without acquiring their writer rights. A cross-Stage reference never grants ownership or permission to edit the supplying Stage.

#### Worker and orchestrator authority

Each Stage candidate has one top-level Codex worker as its sole implementer, writer, focused-test runner and candidate-commit owner inside one isolated worktree. The worker may run fresh read-only reviews after a coherent slice, verifies every finding itself and performs every fix in its own owned paths. It may not edit the canonical design, card, Decisions, shared root facades, dependency lockfiles, canonical generated catalogs, Release manifests, predecessor receipts, `contracts/vnext/**` canonical artifacts, cross-Stage integration tests or final proof publication unless the orchestrator's path manifest assigns that exact file exclusively to the Stage.

The external orchestrator is the sole fanout-base, shared-file, integration-branch, merge, canonical-artifact and seal writer. It verifies the actual base commit and tree, owned-path diff, forbidden-file absence, focused proof, review dispositions and candidate commit rather than trusting worker prose. It integrates one Stage at a time in exact order 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 and 12. Merge conflict, overlapping ownership or a requested shared-interface edit is returned to the owning worker or resolved through a new orchestrator-owned fanout base; the orchestrator never silently combines competing semantics.

A missing interface is `interface_gap`, not permission for a worker to invent a duplicate interface, widen a public contract, edit another Stage or copy semantics into an adapter. If the gap is an implementation omission under an unchanged frozen contract, the orchestrator supplies one owner-local correction and invalidates only candidates whose declared dependency closure changed. If it changes a schema, semantic owner, authority, Action, Resource identity, migration meaning, acceptance or proof obligation, every affected candidate becomes stale and work returns to the required Design, Decision and approval path before further integration.

#### Sequential integration and proof conveyor

For each Stage 6 through 12 in canonical order:

1. the worker rebases or reconstructs its candidate on the exact certified predecessor and resolves implementation-only drift without changing frozen semantics;
2. focused compile, tests, formatting, strict lint, hermeticity, cheap mutant/proof preflight and all fresh read-only reviews pass;
3. the orchestrator verifies path ownership and replaces or parity-proves every fixture/test adapter against the real upstream interface;
4. the broad cross-Stage integration gate runs;
5. the Stage's complete scoped source, test, validator and proof bytes freeze for its broad integration gate;
6. the orchestrator records the passing non-full gate and commits one `integrated_unsealed` recovery checkpoint;
7. the successor may enter canonical integration, but neither checkpoint may claim certification, currentness or release readiness before the final full-chain seal.

Downstream candidate coding and review may continue while this conveyor advances, but canonical merges and broad gates remain one-at-a-time. Later integration that legitimately changes a predecessor-bound source closure must use immutable content-addressed predecessor caching where identity permits and regenerate every affected non-final receipt; cache reuse never replaces independent reexecution required by the final seal. After Stage 12, all bytes freeze once, one cumulative independent multi-engine full-chain seal runs, receipt-bound read-only checks follow, and the final edge sweep verifies the complete integrated tree.

Logical worker concurrency is capped at six. Resource-heavy execution is separately bounded to at most two concurrent compile or focused-test jobs, one broad integration gate and, after Stage 12, one final canonical full-chain seal. Each worktree and independent proof engine uses disjoint temp and target roots. Shared immutable dependency compilation or predecessor caches are reusable only when their complete source, lockfile, toolchain, target, profile, environment and dependency-output identities match; corrupt, substituted or ambiguous cache state fails closed.

The smallest falsifier starts six candidates from one exact fanout base; injects an overlapping path, forbidden shared-file write, upstream implementation-only change, frozen-interface change, stale base, conflicting candidate commit, fixture/real parity mismatch, worker-generated final receipt, premature intermediate full seal, cache substitution and Stage-12 early deletion; and proves respectively refusal or bounded invalidation with zero false certification. It then integrates 6 through 12 sequentially, proves every original Stage gate at its owning checkpoint and reproduces every required case and receipt ancestry in the one final full-chain result. Reopen this execution overlay if a Stage cannot be implemented behind its frozen interface without copying owner semantics, a real upstream adapter cannot replace its test adapter locally, path ownership cannot remain disjoint, later source necessarily invalidates already certified semantics rather than proof ancestry alone, or six logical workers cannot be scheduled without weakening hermeticity or independent final proof.

The following compact slice/proof view uses the same Stage 0..12 namespace and cannot rename, reorder or redefine a stage. Delivery sequencing and deferred full reexecution never reduce the full product target.

#### Manifest identity and catalog bytes

Effective Decision: `dec-canonical-manifestidentityv1-byte-729e`. This is a candidate Contract Component and creates no runtime authority before publication.

Choose the strict byte-identity profile. ManifestIdentityV1 is the sole design-time and runtime identity protocol for every vNext schema, descriptor, census and manifest named by this refoundation. It uses SHA-256 over the RFC 8949 deterministic-CBOR subset frozen here. Hashed values may contain only nonnegative integers, booleans, raw byte strings, ASCII UTF-8 text and definite-length arrays. Maps, tags, null, floats, negative integers, indefinite lengths, non-ASCII text and implicit Unicode normalization are forbidden. Integers and lengths use the shortest permitted encoding. Arrays preserve schema order. Every set-like sequence declares one exact sort key and rejects duplicate keys before hashing. Optional values encode only as [0] for absent or [1,value] for present, so absent, empty and zero are distinct.

SchemaDescriptorV1 is the bootstrap fixed array [schema_id_ascii, schema_version_u64, fields, cross_constraints], where fields is strictly position-sorted and each field is [position_u64, field_name_ascii, type_expr, constraints]. Field positions and field names are each unique. TypeExprV1 is the closed tagged array union: [1] unsigned integer; [2] boolean; [3] ASCII text; [4,n] exact-length bytes; [5,schema_id_ascii,version,referenced_schema_id_bytes32] content-bound schema reference; [6,type] optional; [7,type] ordered list; [8,types] tuple; [9,enum_id,[[numeric_tag,name]...]] closed enum. Inline enum rows are strictly tag-sorted with unique positive tags and unique ASCII names. FieldPathV1 is one nonempty definite array of PathStepV1. PathStepV1 is exactly [1,field_position_u64] for a SchemaDescriptor field or [2,tuple_index_u64] for a zero-based tuple member. Paths are validated against the traversed TypeExpr and never traverse an optional value without presence; a canonical-set key path is evaluated relative to each list element and must terminate at TypeExpr [1], an unsigned integer. ConstraintExprV1 is the closed tagged union: [1] no additional constraint; [2,min_count,max_count] bounded length; [3,FieldPathV1,min_count,max_count] canonical set sorted strictly by the terminal unsigned key with duplicate-key rejection; [4,min_u64,max_u64] unsigned range; [5,FieldPathV1] exact field equality. Constraint [1] is valid only as the sole constraint. Every minimum is less than or equal to its maximum. Constraint [3] applies only to TypeExpr [7]. CrossConstraintExprV1 is the closed tagged union: [1,left_path,right_path] equality; [2,[field_paths]] exactly one present; [3,[field_paths]] all present or all absent. Exactly-one and all-or-none paths must target optional fields. Every field carries a nonempty constraint list, so ordered-list versus canonical-set semantics, uniqueness, sort key and finite bounds are content-bound. Per-field constraint lists and cross_constraints are sorted strictly by their deterministic-CBOR bytes with duplicate rejection; every embedded set of FieldPathV1 values is sorted lexicographically by encoded path with duplicate rejection. Field positions and enum tags are positive, stable and never reused. Schema-reference graphs are finite and acyclic in V1; every referenced SchemaId is recomputed before use, and one dependency closure permits exactly one SchemaId for each (schema_id_ascii,schema_version) pair. Unknown types or constraints, invalid paths, dangling or cyclic schema references, duplicate positions/names/tags, unsorted sets or unsupported schema versions fail closed.

SchemaIdV1 is raw SHA-256 of deterministic CBOR ["maestro.vnext.schema.v1", SchemaDescriptorV1]. DescriptorIdV1 is raw SHA-256 of deterministic CBOR [descriptor_domain_tag_ascii, SchemaIdV1_bytes32, descriptor_value]. ManifestValueV1 is the typed array [manifest_header_value, rows]. Each catalog freezes its own content-bound ManifestHeader schema. Every header binds catalog/core/canonicalization versions, generated-sum SchemaId, exact dependency ManifestIds and protocol hashes, owner-protocol hashes, row count, finite bounds, and migration/parity/removal/proof profile identities required by that catalog. ManifestIdV1 is raw SHA-256 of deterministic CBOR [manifest_domain_tag_ascii, manifest_schema_id_bytes32, descriptor_schema_id_bytes32, manifest_header_value, rows]. Each row is exactly [numeric_tag,DescriptorIdV1_bytes32,descriptor_value]. Rows sort strictly by numeric tag; every tag is nonzero, unique, within the header bound, and exactly equals the descriptor value's declared tag. Verification recomputes every DescriptorId and both SchemaIds before the ManifestId. Human renderings use lowercase `sha256:` plus 64 hexadecimal digits, but the hashed envelope always carries raw 32-byte digests. No schema, descriptor, header or row may embed its containing ManifestId, any value derived from it, a future root, latest selector, request, Receipt, Result or current Head. The dependency graph is finite and strictly backward: no forward hash dependency or self-hash is permitted.

The fixed descriptor/manifest domain-tag pairs are: maestro.vnext.observation-kind.descriptor.v1 / maestro.vnext.observation-kind.manifest.v1; maestro.vnext.effect-origin.descriptor.v1 / maestro.vnext.effect-origin.manifest.v1; maestro.vnext.action-leaf.descriptor.v1 / maestro.vnext.action-leaf-census.manifest.v1; maestro.vnext.governed-capacity.repository.descriptor.v1 / maestro.vnext.governed-capacity.repository.manifest.v1; maestro.vnext.governed-capacity.installation.descriptor.v1 / maestro.vnext.governed-capacity.installation.manifest.v1; maestro.vnext.ceremony-spec.descriptor.v1 / maestro.vnext.ceremony-spec.manifest.v1; maestro.vnext.authority-continuity.repository.descriptor.v1 / maestro.vnext.authority-continuity.repository.manifest.v1; maestro.vnext.authority-continuity.installation.descriptor.v1 / maestro.vnext.authority-continuity.installation.manifest.v1; and maestro.vnext.action-spec.descriptor.v1 / maestro.vnext.action-spec.catalog.v1. Domain tags are protocol constants and cannot be supplied by a caller, adapter, extension or migrated artifact.

Every later catalog Decision must publish its literal SchemaDescriptorV1 values, manifest-header value, descriptor rows, full canonical CBOR bytes as lowercase hexadecimal, byte length, SHA-256 digest and computed IDs, plus two independent reference-encoder equality receipts. A mismatch is an integrity failure, not an alternate valid encoding. Migration preserves source bytes and recomputes vNext identities only from admitted typed values; legacy hashes, JSON key order, text normalization, object paths and prior content addresses never become vNext identity. Adapter rendering is non-authoritative and must round-trip to the same typed value. Reopen only if two conforming independent encoders disagree on the frozen subset, SHA-256 becomes disallowed by the product security baseline, or a required closed semantic value cannot be represented without a new versioned TypeExpr or ConstraintExpr and full manifest regeneration.

##### Efa0 successor identity law over unchanged 7138 public transport and incorporated H2/H3

The predecessor grammar and nine catalog generations remain immutable evidence but are not current candidate identities. D116 preserves the exact 7138 public Integration manifest, `McpPacketReadRequestV1`, `McpPacketReadEnvelopeV1`, AgentPacket binding/provenance schemas, two MCP descriptors, CLI Capability Catalog meaning, Skill/bootstrap references and Packet/Recipe semantics; d21e adds only its four internal H2 components; 3905 adds the H3 withdrawal grammar and 139 semantic effect-route tuples; and a13b adds the owner-joined SubmissionClaimSet dependency. Efa0 preserves those public bytes, H2/H3 meanings and 139 route semantics while closing the lifecycle-to-Action map and owner partition. The current GrammarId therefore encodes nine route roles, 139 routes, two Action reservation modes, four Ceremony request modes, the unchanged 28-edge DAG, 145 Action symbols, eleven Ceremony symbols and twenty-one profiles. Relative to 3905/d0aa, the current set adds six ActionLeaf and six ActionSpec descriptors, moves existing `SubmitStep` ownership from Execution to Step, changes the Work/Step/Execution profiles, and retains `Withdraw` on all eleven Ceremony descriptors, the exact 23-origin route relation, the Bootstrap terminal-scope exclusion and five CMA `EffectWithdrawal` slot families. Both 145-row manifests, the 139-route Manifest identity, every catalog Header and all nine ManifestIds rotate; exact tags and complete rotation remain Stage-0 outputs, so no otherwise unchanged profile or row is asserted byte-stable. Every dependency-bound c868, Release, Resource, Receipt, Bundle, Census, 65b3 writer-compat, candidate-root and Handoff identity is recomputed with two independent encoders and one independent semantic validator. Separately retain 7138's internal Execution-owned Home/fence schemas, compatibility relation and cohorts, the Step-owned retain-initialization schema and satisfaction-carry matrix, d116 same-Attempt recovery, d21e's Execution-owned Head/revision/transition/writer-term algebra and a13b's SubmissionClaimSet algebra. Any unenumerated, inferred or mismatched delta, any old/current or mixed 147/150/156 material, any failure to reproduce d70b/d0aa/d116/H2/H3 evidence, or any fabricated Stage-0 byte blocks admission.

### Governance, locator, census and finality successor amendment

This section is the current external-build design head. It is an additive
successor amendment to every unaffected clause above and rotates the frozen
Stage-5 internal interface boundary before any new implementation or proof
publication. It changes no Action, owner tag, public or persisted schema,
Catalog member, Resource, Bundle, Release, wire representation or canonical
identity algorithm. Where this section expressly supersedes an older production
materialization seam, the older Decision remains immutable predecessor evidence
and its unaffected laws remain normative.

#### Locked Decision order and common capability law

The following four Decisions were opened and locked in this exact order:

1. `dec-canonical-authority-owned-governance-c77d`, **Canonical Authority-owned Governance Attestation**.
2. `dec-canonical-persistence-owned-protected-ca82`, **Canonical Persistence-owned Protected Locator Lease**.
3. `dec-canonical-foundation-owned-aggregate-f9e7`, **Canonical Foundation-owned Aggregate Census Lease**.
4. `dec-canonical-installation-owned-durable-f439`, **Canonical Installation-owned Durable Finality Provider**.

Every capability introduced by these Decisions is process-local, owner-minted,
move-only, non-cloneable, non-serializable, non-cacheable, non-replayable and
non-transferable. Each has private fields, a private constructor and a
non-static owner-operation lifetime. None has a public or crate-wide
constructor, `Copy`, `Clone`, `Default`, `Debug`, `Send`, `Sync`, `'static`
escape, bearer accessor, downcast or conversion, canonical bytes, persistence,
registry, cache, log form, Resource identity, wire representation, restart
reconstruction or hidden global lookup. Capability replay is forbidden while
exact committed-Result idempotency replay remains required.

Authority alone derives and atomically rechecks the live Repository Governance
Floor object and Action-105 requirement. It separately validates the Scheduling
Safety Floor's pinned policy-diff classifier; neither namespace may substitute
for the other. Planning supplies only nominal typed policy and safety facts and
cannot supply governance ids, revisions, requirements, classifier selection or
result, downgrade route, raw floor values, currentness, revocation or parsed
Authority state. The new `GovernanceAttestationV1<'tx>` joins rather than
replaces the existing scheduling-downgrade Mandate use and sealed repository
Action binding.

Persistence owns the real protected-locator observation and
`ProtectedLocatorLeaseV1<'locator>`. The lease retains the exact facility,
provider incarnation, external anchor and backend handle; binds Realm, locator
slot, root, CAS token/version/incarnation, Ceremony, Attempt, carrier,
anti-rollback and currentness; and performs full-tuple rereads before dispatch
and during final resolution. Callers provide no root, path, raw CAS, count,
absence claim, final candidate root or seal as evidence. Candidate root and seal
are derived only after inert association materialization. Exact post-dispatch
readback distinguishes committed, `recovery_required`, `in_doubt` and
integrity-blocked outcomes without blind retry.

Foundation owns one `AggregateCensusLeaseV1<'scan>` and one
single-consumption sealed result across the complete admitted root capability
set. This expressly supersedes the production singular-root cardinality, lease
and finality clauses of `dec-canonical-foundation-descriptor-a128`; the older
descriptor-relative no-follow, same-mount descendant, single-link leaf,
lossless-locator, zero-partial-result and physical-ownership laws remain
unchanged. All root handles and component fences remain live simultaneously
through pass A over all roots, the complete scan, pass B over all roots and one
coherent final cross-root recheck. Optional-root membership drift, overlap,
physical aliasing, mutation, replacement, ABA, mount/provider change,
component-fence loss or aggregate overflow fails the whole census with zero
rows.

Installation owns
`DurableInstallationFinalityBackendV1<'effect>`, which captures one
owner-bound durable effect provider inside a nominal ActiveStore or PreStore
backend. ActiveStore performs the exact same-domain atomic Store commit and
owner-local postcondition readback; acknowledgement loss is resolved by exact
idempotency and readback, never post-write refusal or blind retry. PreStore is
strictly inert: it performs no Store, network, locator or currentness mutation,
and only validates the already materialized association, consumer commitment,
candidate root, seal, Ceremony, Attempt, carrier and postcondition while
joining the live protected-locator lease. The existing Ceremony owner alone
dispatches and resolves the protected CAS. No caller callback, ambient Store,
registry or hidden lookup may act as a finality provider.

#### Rotated Stage-5 frozen interface boundary

The Stage-5 source boundary must now freeze exactly four owner-private,
non-static seams and their test-only conformance adapters:

| Frozen Stage-5 seam | Owner and minter | Exact later production obligation |

| `GovernanceAttestationV1<'tx>` plus consuming scheduling-publication continuation | Authority | Stage 7 replaces the provisional caller governance tuple with typed Planning facts and Authority-owned derivation and coherent final recheck |
| `ProtectedLocatorLeaseV1<'locator>` plus Installation acquisition and consuming PreStore-finality port | Persistence owns physical currentness and minting; Installation owns operation composition | Stage 9 supplies the real protected-locator provider; Stage 11 consumes it only through the frozen owner operation |
| `AggregateCensusLeaseV1<'scan>` plus sealed single-consumption result | Foundation | Stage 11 replaces the singular production path with the complete admitted-root operation and a supported-platform aggregate backend |
| `DurableInstallationFinalityBackendV1<'effect>` with captured ActiveStore/PreStore provider variants | Installation | Stages 9 and 11 provide real context-specific operations; ActiveStore owns atomic effect/readback and PreStore remains inert |

All four Stage-5 conformance adapters are test-only and fail closed outside
their exact fixtures. They do not attest production provenance, Store
finality, protected-locator currentness or platform-wide census currentness.
The frozen seam may use private nominal carrier types but may not expose public
or persistent schemas, add an Action, alter the 145-Action/444-row catalog, or
duplicate Stage-7, Stage-9 or Stage-11 product behavior.

`dec-canonical-authority-owned-persisted-454e`, **Canonical Authority-owned

Governance and Scheduling Safety remain separate namespaces. The persisted

### Final closure successor amendment

This section is the current external-build design head. It is authorized by the
exact user-role event `APPROVE SUCCESSOR DESIGN PASS.` in recipient task
`019f8416-e121-7703-8ab4-d3f9c3b374fa`. It opens no product implementation,
generates no canonical contract artifact and runs no seal. Every unaffected
prior Decision and semantic law remains normative. The following three
Decisions were opened and locked in exact order after independent adversarial
review:

1. `dec-canonical-foundation-owned-admitted-d215`, **Canonical
   Foundation-owned admitted-root source and aggregate census V2**, superseding
   the production contract of
   `dec-canonical-foundation-owned-aggregate-f9e7`.
2. `dec-canonical-pre-candidate-protected-370d`, **Canonical pre-candidate
   protected locator and durable finality V2**, superseding
   `dec-canonical-persistence-owned-protected-ca82` and
   `dec-canonical-installation-owned-durable-f439`.
3. `dec-canonical-final-cumulative-stage-0-1652`, **Canonical final cumulative
   Stage 0 through 12 seal contract**, additive and authoritative over prior
   execution-only Stage-seal scheduling text.

Every V2 capability obeys the common rule already locked for successor
materialization: owner-minted, process-local, move-only, non-cloneable,
non-serializable, non-cacheable, non-replayable, non-Send, non-Sync,
non-transferable, private constructor, non-static lifetime, no public or
crate-wide constructor, no raw scalar or physical-locator accessor, no
canonical bytes, persistence, Resource identity, registry, wire
representation, restart reconstruction or hidden global lookup. Exact
committed-Result idempotency replay remains required and is checked before
capability acquisition.

#### Foundation admitted-root source V2

Persistence is the sole source of then-live RepositoryDomain root admission and
Installation is the sole source of then-live InstallationDomain root
admission. Foundation invokes both private owner ports from one
physical-scope-free `CensusInvocationV2` and consumes the two one-use admissions
into `FoundationAdmittedRootSourceV2`. The source binds the complete union,
canonical domain/root order, retained physical handles or protected locators,
optionality, semantic association tokens,
provider/incarnation/currentness/revocation and replacement/ABA fences.
Migration supplies no path, root list, membership, optionality, count, absence
claim, locator, digest, epoch, backend selector or parsed owner state.

Foundation retains every root handle and fence simultaneously through both
complete passes, the recursive byte-total scan, cross-root alias and overlap
resolution, aggregate limits and one final cross-root recheck. Unsupported or
incomplete owner providers make production success unavailable. Failure of any
root, owner source or fence returns zero rows and zero Migration effect.

Migration receives only a sealed classification continuation over bounded
`MigrationClassifiableRootViewV2` values keyed by opaque
`RootAssociationTokenV2`. It cannot select or enumerate physical scope.
Foundation, Persistence and Installation later join physical commitments with
Migration-owned nominal classifications behind an owner-private V2 inventory
builder. The Migration-built `DeclaredRootScanV1` and
`Vec<DeclaredRootV1>` production path becomes historical/test-only negative
evidence. No new persisted schema, public schema, Action, Resource, Bundle,
Release or catalog member is introduced; crash recovery reacquires fresh live
owner sources.

#### Protected locator and durable finality V2

`ProtectedLocatorAcquisitionRequestV2` is created before association, candidate
root/carrier/seal, CAS or finality backend. It contains only nominal
authenticated operation identity and no caller-supplied locator observation or
candidate evidence. Persistence acquires the real no-follow locator and mints
`ProtectedLocatorLeaseV2` before all candidate derivation. Installation retains
that lease through inert association and candidate construction, derives one
private `ProtectedLocatorCandidateTransitionV2` and gives only that transition

an internal descriptor-schema rotation, not a public Packet, API, Tool, Action
or catalog delta. The current `agents-compatible-cli` and `claude-code`
profiles have no packet-proven provider factory or injection contract and
therefore publish V2 `Inactive`. Ordinary exact-two MCP transport may run
without that provider, but it cannot claim protected authentication.

The second successor makes the already frozen public MCP catalog real:
`maestro_packet` and `maestro_cli_search`, in that order, with no third Tool,
legacy alias, hidden registry, deprecated dispatch or adapter-private list.
Every list, dispatch, descriptor, generated catalog, host profile, schema,
test and final census derives or parity-proves that exact pair.
`maestro_packet` requires one explicit alias-closed `repository_locator` and
never discovers a repository from cwd. `maestro_cli_search` searches only the
catalog embedded in the running installed binary and opens no repository,
Store, legacy catalog or ambient filesystem root.

Every legacy MCP name fails as unknown before repository discovery, Store
access, Projection invocation, mutation, cache, network, translation or
fallback. The existing broad tests that assert 42 MCP Tools or
`maestro_status` do not become compatibility exceptions. Their underlying
product cases move to owning CLI, domain or operation suites, while MCP tests
rotate to exact-two enumeration, explicit-locator/no-cwd behavior,
coarse-unavailable protected access without injection, supported-provider
parity when one exists, legacy-name pre-effect refusal, protocol errors,
batching and zero hidden registry. A replacement test mapping is mandatory;
removing a legacy MCP assertion cannot remove the behavior proof it formerly
carried.

These Decisions add no Action, ScopeAtom, Ceremony, Grant, Mandate, Receipt,
Result, Observation, Evidence, public successor member, Resource, Recipe,
Bundle, Release, public schema member or wire field. They preserve every V6
Migration, quarantine, rollback, removal, primary-protection and final-seal
law not explicitly superseded above.
